articles.title: P12.2M in presidential aid released to 61 Bacolod villages
articles.summary: BACOLOD CITY - This highly-urbanized city has released P12.2 million in financial assistance under President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.'s "Bawat Barangay Makikinabang” (BBM) program to 61 barangays for…

blocks.text: BACOLOD CITY - This highly-urbanized city has released P12.2 million in financial assistance under President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.'s "Bawat Barangay Makikinabang” (BBM) program to 61
barangays for their socio-civic projects.

Bacolod City Mayor Greg Gasataya, in coordination with the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) and the Office of the President, led the distribution of checks to representatives of all barangays during a recent ceremonial turnover at the Bacolod City Government Center (BCGC) lobby.

Each barangay received a total allocation of P200,000, which included P100,000 for five Presidential Scholars, and P100,000 for a community development project identified by the barangay. Each scholar received P20,000 in educational assistance.
Gasataya thanked the President and the national government for extending the program to all barangays, acknowledging the urgency and necessity of this program.
He said this is the first time the national government has equally provided the Local Government Support Fund (LGSF) to all barangays, regardless of population and size.

Gasataya also thanked barangay officials for their cooperation in completing the requirements necessary for the release of the funds, emphasizing that the program is intended to directly benefit their constituents.
He required all barangay captains to submit signed certifications attesting that none of their selected scholars are family members or relatives of any incumbent barangay official.
“This is to ensure that those who will benefit from the scholarship program are the ones who need it most,” the mayor stressed.
DILG City Director Christian Nagaynay emphasized that accountability and transparency remain central to the program’s implementation.

He noted that barangays are required to publicly post information on the distribution of assistance, including aid provided to scholars, and submit a fund utilization report every 30 days for the community projects they implement.

The city government reaffirmed its commitment to working closely with barangay officials and national government agencies to ensure that the funds are utilized properly, efficiently, and transparently.

articles.title: June Mar Fajardo retires confident Gilas Pilipinas is in good hands
articles.summary: June Mar Fajardo draws the curtain on a 13-year Gilas Pilipinas career, grateful to have played alongside its pioneers, been part of the present, and shared the court with the future of the national…

blocks.text: VETERAN. June Mar Fajardo in action for Gilas Pilipinas in the FIBA World Cup 2027 Asian Qualifiers.
FIBA

June Mar Fajardo draws the curtain on a 13-year Gilas Pilipinas career, grateful to have played alongside its pioneers, been part of the present, and shared the court with the future of the national team
MANILA, Philippines – There is obviously still plenty of gas left in the tank for June Mar Fajardo, but he wants to end his Gilas Pilipinas career on his own terms.

Fajardo, 36, donned the national colors for the final time, helping the Philippines claim a pivotal 68-56 win over rival Iran in the fourth window of the FIBA World Cup Asian Qualifiers on Sunday, August 30.
“This is really my last game,” Fajardo confirmed after taking a bow at center court of the Mall of Asia Arena before an adoring home crowd.

blocks.caption: June Mar Fajardo retires confident Gilas Pilipinas is in good hands

blocks.text: And Fajardo went out in style as he finished with 6 points and 2 rebounds — his contributions in the second quarter allowing the Nationals to erase a double-digit deficit as they beat Iran in FIBA play for the first time in over a decade.

Fajardo converted his lone field goal attempt and sank all four of his free throws in just a little over seven minutes of action before spending most of the rest of the game on the bench, proudly watching the young guns steer the team safely to victory.
“Whatever I can contribute, I’ll give. I want to cherish my last game,” he said.
Fajardo draws the curtain on a 13-year national team career highlighted by three World Cup appearances and gold medals in the Asian Games, Southeast Asian Games, and SEABA Championship.

He is the last remnant of the iconic team that ended the Philippines’ curse against South Korea in the semifinals of the 2013 FIBA Asia Championship — a victory that sent the country to the World Cup for the first time in nearly four decades.
“I feel so blessed to have played with the pioneers of Gilas, to have played with the present generation, and to have played with the future of Gilas,” said Fajardo.

Once the youngest but now the oldest member of the squad, Fajardo said he is walking away from the national team to preserve his body, knowing that international competition becomes increasingly demanding with age.
He is also keen on winning more championships with San Miguel in the PBA.
“I don’t want to push my body to its limit. I still want to play basketball. I’m still enjoying the game, but I won’t be able to enjoy it if I’m playing through pain,” said Fajardo.
Fajardo knows the national team is in good hands, with Kai Sotto, Dwight Ramos, AJ Edu, Kevin Quiambao, Carl Tamayo, and Juan Gomez de Liaño forming a formidable foundation for Gilas’ next era.
“The future is very bright for Gilas. We can all see that,” he said. – Rappler.com

blocks.text: Police in Bonn say they have been investigating the wreckage of a car found in the Rhine River in the Königswinter area this month.
The stricken vehicle was first spotted in early August as the river levels nosedived in the protracted dry hot weather.
Two weeks after it was seen, the fire department was able to recover the vehicle. Inside it, and near to it, the remains of human bones were discovered.
Police said they were trying to investigate the backdrop of the case, but said that as yet there were no leads on potential missing persons cases that could be connected to the car.

Police believe the car, thought to be a Fiat produced at some point between 1976 and 1984, could have been lying on the riverbed for decades. It was not yet clear whether the fragments of bones hailed from one person or more than one.
"The investigations are proving difficult, because it's so far in the past," a police spokesman told the German DPA news agency.
Königswinter lies just south of Bonn on the right bank of the Rhine.

articles.title: Man who threw deceased dog into Marikina River to face raps — mayor
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Marikina City Mayor Maan Teodoro assured the public that the individual who threw a sack reportedly containing a deceased dog into the Marikina River will face appropriate…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Marikina City Mayor Maan Teodoro assured the public that the individual who threw a sack reportedly containing a deceased dog into the Marikina River will face appropriate charges.
Teodoro was referring to the man in a viral Facebook video uploaded on Sunday, which showed him dumping the sack into the river despite the uploader’s plea not to do so.
After throwing the sack supposedly containing the dog’s body, the man only smiled and then walked away.
As of this writing, the video had already garnered around 9,000 reactions and 1,700 shares, with netizens calling the attention of Teodoro and animal group advocates.
In a comment updated on Monday, Teodoro said they had already located the man in the video.
“Sasampahan [siya] ng kaukulang reklamo,” Teodoro said, but did not yet indicate the charges that will be filed against the individual.
(An appropriate complaint will be filed against him.)
“Ipinapaubaya na natin sa mga rightful authorities ang proseso ng hustisya,” she added.
(We are leaving the justice process to the proper authorities.)
The Marikina mayor described the man’s conduct as “rude” and “disgusting,” noting that the dog was “defenseless.”
“Hindi ‘yan katanggap-tanggap at hindi natin palalampasin ‘yan sa Marikina,” said Teodoro.
(That is unacceptable and we will not let this happen in Marikina.) /mr

articles.title: Palace says Ombudsman probe into flood mess should not be rushed
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Malacañang on Monday said the Office of the Ombudsman should be allowed to take its time in investigating the flood control mess, warning that rushing cases could result in…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Malacañang on Monday said the Office of the Ombudsman should be allowed to take its time in investigating the flood control mess, warning that rushing cases could result in insufficient evidence and their eventual dismissal.
In a video statement, Palace press officer Claire Castro emphasized that the Office of the Ombudsman is an independent body with its own mandate.
“Mahirap madaliin ang kaso tapos hilaw. Sisisihin sila kapag na dismiss ang kaso dahil kulang sa ebidensiya,” she said, explaining why the probe should be allowed to run its course.
(It is difficult to rush a case and end up with an incomplete one. They will be blamed if the case is dismissed due to insufficient evidence.)

“So, hayaan po natin magtrabaho ang Ombudsman dahil alam po nila ang kanilang responsabilidad. At nakikita po naman natin ang kanilang pag-aaral, pag-iimbestiga ay naaayon naman po sa proseso,” Castro continued.
(So, let us allow the Ombudsman to do its job because they know their responsibilities. We can also see that their review and investigation are being conducted in accordance with due process.)

Castro said she understands the difficulty of going through mountains of files related to the flood control mess, adding that the Office of the Ombudsman also wants to expedite the cases under investigation.

“Nadidinig naman po natin ang mga report, mga salita, ang mga mensahe ni ombudsman Boying Rimulia kung paano sila nang tatrabaho at paano nila inaaral ang mga naipasa na mga dokumento sa kanilang opisina,” Castro said.
(We have heard the reports, statements, and messages from Ombudsman Boying Remulla on how they are working and reviewing the documents submitted to their office.)

The Office of the Ombudsman is leading the nationwide investigation, case buildup, and filing of charges against public officials and individuals involved in the multi-billion-peso government flood control project anomalies.

Last week, it filed a second malversation case against former Ako Bicol party-list Rep. Zaldy Co before the Sandiganbayan over an alleged nonexistent P77-million flood control project in Balagtas, Bulacan.

The six-page case information was filed before the anti-graft court on August 28 for one count each of malversation of public funds and one count each of violation of Republic Act No. 3019, or the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act against Co as well as former Department of Public Works and Highways officials Brice Hernandez, Arjay Salvador Domasig, Jaypee De Leon Mendoza, Niño Lawrence Vergara Morales, Juanito Coronel Mendoza, Floralyn Yutuc Simbulan and Christina Mae Del Rosario Pineda.

Meanwhile, Remulla recently said the anti-graft body is investigating possible corruption in flood control projects in Davao City, which he described as the “epicenter” of budget allocations during the previous administration. /mr

articles.title: Palace warns of jail for stealing pumping station parts
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Malacañang on Monday warned that people stealing components from government pumping stations could land in jail, saying the theft could delay floodwaters from receding and put…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Malacañang on Monday warned that people stealing components from government pumping stations could land in jail, saying the theft could delay floodwaters from receding and put lives and property at risk.

Palace press officer Claire Castro said President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. had directed the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) and the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) to prevent the theft of pumping station components and ensure the facilities remain operational.

“To all those committing these acts of sabotage, you will be pursued by the law. We will hold you accountable because lives and livelihoods could be affected by your selfish acts,” she said in a video message sent to reporters.
She appealed to the public not to sabotage the government’s flood control efforts.
“What the president is doing against flooding is for all of us. Let us not be selfish,” Castro said. “Let us help one another. We are all Filipinos.”

According to Castro, the Marcos administration took pride in ensuring that pumping stations and other flood mitigation structures had been repaired and restored to operate efficiently before the start of the rainy season.
Castro claimed the rehabilitated flood-control projects helped accelerate the reduction of floodwaters in parts of Metro Manila despite heavy and continuous rains in recent weeks.
However, stealing parts and components of pumping stations could render them useless in preventing floods.

Castro said the government would also have to spend again to replace the stolen components. Delays in securing replacement parts could further postpone repairs and, consequently, prolong flooding in affected areas.

During his inspection on Sunday, DPWH Secretary Vince Dizon found that high-voltage cables at the Sunog Apog pumping station in Tondo, Manila, had been stolen, rendering the facility inoperative since Saturday, at the height of heavy rains and flooding in Metro Manila.
Marcos led an inspection of the P774-million pumping station in May to ensure that it was fully operational by the start of the rainy season in June, after six years of being non-operational.

The Sunog Apog pumping station is part of the government’s long-term solution to perennial flooding in the low-lying areas of España, Sampaloc, Rizal Avenue and Maria Clara Street in Manila, as well as some parts of Quezon City.
Replacement cables were installed, restoring the pumping station’s operation on Sunday.
Dizon also revealed that heavy-duty check valves, crucial for preventing backflow from the swollen Marikina River, were pilfered from the Tumana pumping station.
Iron manhole covers along Roxas Boulevard were also taken, triggering car accidents on the major thoroughfare.

Marcos earlier announced that the government would add 13 pumping stations to the 73 currently managed by the Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) as long-term solutions to address flooding in Metro Manila.
Of the 13, four will be brand new, while the rest will be upgrades to existing facilities. The additional pumping stations should be operational by the end of the year or early 2027. /mcm

articles.title: Manila logs 33 new flu-like cases amid habagat rains, floods
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The local government of Manila recorded 33 new cases of influenza-like illness (ILI) on Monday, Aug. 31, its Public Information Office (PIO) said. The latest WILD diseases…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The local government of Manila recorded 33 new cases of influenza-like illness (ILI) on Monday, Aug. 31, its Public Information Office (PIO) said.
The latest WILD diseases report showed that the new cases brought the city’s total number of ILI cases to 1,203 since the start of the year.
W.I.L.D. stands for illnesses that commonly surge during the rainy season: water-borne diseases, influenza, leptospirosis and dengue.
On Aug. 31, the city also recorded 24 new dengue cases, bringing the total to 2,541, and four new cases of leptospirosis, bringing the total to 556.
No new cases were reported for the other diseases, like cholera, typhoid fever, COVID-19, and severe acute respiratory infection.
The Manila PIO urged residents to practice proper hygiene and seek medical attention promptly if they experience any symptoms. /mr

articles.title: DA: El Niño puts food supply under pressure
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Agriculture (DA) is updating its response plans for the developing El Niño as drought threatens domestic crop production and could put pressure on food supply…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Agriculture (DA) is updating its response plans for the developing El Niño as drought threatens domestic crop production and could put pressure on food supply and prices.
Agriculture Secretary Francisco Tiu Laurel Jr. has directed DA agencies to continuously adjust their plans as new weather, crop, water, and market data become available, the agency said.

The move comes after the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas warned that El Niño could fuel inflation, adding to concerns over food supply at a time when global rice markets remain exposed to weather disruptions and changes in trade policies.
“The lessons we learned from the powerful El Niño episode that ended in mid-2024 should help us respond better to the climate challenge we now face,” Tiu Laurel said in a statement on Sunday.

The DA chief said the agency is working on immediate assistance for local producers while also preparing measures to secure food supplies before weather disruptions lead to shortages and higher prices.
He added that the government also plans to shift production toward areas expected to be less affected by El Niño, expand cloud seeding and solar-powered irrigation, and improve water-use efficiency.
The measures include distributing drought-tolerant seeds, providing crop insurance indemnification and extending emergency financial assistance to vulnerable farmers.

“We have to produce more where the impact of El Niño will be less severe, increase the water available to farmers, and use every drop wisely through practices such as alternate wetting and drying and planting crops that require less water,” he said. /mcm

articles.title: Allegations against Romualdez ‘no longer credible,’ says lawyer
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Retired marine Orly Guteza’s recantation of his original testimony involving the flood control scandal has undermined the allegations of the remaining 14 Maleta Boys, making it…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Retired marine Orly Guteza’s recantation of his original testimony involving the flood control scandal has undermined the allegations of the remaining 14 Maleta Boys, making it no longer credible, a public interest and human rights lawyer said.

Litigation lawyer Antonio “Audie” Bucoy made the pronouncement in defense of former Speaker Martin Romualdez, who he claimed was being targeted by the Ombudsman amid its supposed 42 witnesses against the lawmaker.

“Hindi ito laban ng paramihan ng testigo eh. Ito ay labanan ng kredibilidad at kalidad ng testigo. Gaya ng 18 (Maleta Boys), apat ang tumuligsa diyan. Pero pinanindigan nung apat kung bakit hindi totoo ‘yung mga sinabi nila noon,” he said in a dzMM interview over the weekend.

(This isn’t a battle of who has more witnesses. It is a battle regarding the credibility and quality of the witnesses. Take the Maleta Boy case, for instance, four people testified against the accused there. Yet, those four later stood by their statements explaining why what they had said previously was untrue.)

Bucoy was referring to Guteza and some of the 18 bodyguards who recanted their statements claiming they delivered money to lawmakers, particularly funds that supposedly came from resigned lawmaker Zaldy Co, who served as chairperson of the House committee on appropriations during the 19th Congress.
However, Bucon noted that the most important retraction was from Guteza, who also happened to be the first to make allegations against Romualdez in a Senate blue ribbon committee hearing.
“Kung maalala niyo, ang una hong lumutang diyan ay si Orly Guteza. Nung bigla siyang naglaho ng hindi pa siya nasusuri ng mahusay, lumutang bigla yung 18,” Bucoy added.
(If you recall, the first person to surface in that matter was Orly Guteza. When he suddenly disappeared before he could be thoroughly examined, the 18 suddenly surfaced.

The lawyer then asserted that the allegations of Guteza and the 18 Maleta Boys were interconnected, and with Guteza’s retraction, supported by the assertions of 25 former Co aides, there is no more evidence against Romualdez.

“Kung pinabulaanan na ni Orly Guteza yung kanyang unang salaysay at sinabing ito ay pinilit lamang sa kanya at merong panunuhol na kaakibat ito, dagdag pa natin yung sinabi nung 25 na tinuligsa rin yung 18, ano pang kalalabasan nito? Wala hong ebidensiya. Hindi kapani-paniwala yung natitira,” he said.

(If Orly Guteza has already retracted his initial statement, claiming he was coerced into making it and that bribery was involved, and we also consider the testimony of the “25” who denounced the 18, what does that leave us with? There is no evidence. What remains is simply not credible.)

Furthermore, Bucoy claimed the Ombudsman is resorting to selective prosecution of those allegedly involved in the flood control scam, specifically Romualdez, as the original allegations of the 18 Maleta Boys were directed not only against him but other lawmakers and public officials as well.
“Namimili sila kung alin ang gagamiting ebidensiya, alin ang hindi at kung ating maaalala, yun hong testimonya 18, hindi lang naman si dating Speaker Romualdez ang tinukoy dito eh,” he said.
(They are selecting which evidence to use and which not to; and if we recall, regarding Testimony 18, it wasn’t just former Speaker Romualdez who was identified there.)
Office of the Ombudsman investigators cited Guteza’s testimony in the supplemental complaint-affidavit for plunder, direct bribery, graft and corruption against Romualdez and Co. /mr

articles.title: Marcos allies say OP's P4.5B proposed confi, intel fund for 2027 justified
articles.summary: House good government and public accountability panel vice chairperson Benny Abante on Monday defended President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos, Jr."s proposed P4.5 billion confidential and intelligence…

blocks.text: House good government and public accountability panel vice chairperson Benny Abante on Monday defended President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos, Jr.’s proposed P4.5 billion confidential and intelligence fund (CIF) for 2027.

“I think we have to remember that the President is also the commander-in-chief of the Armed Forces. Therefore, he has all the right to have a confidential fund,” Abante said during an online press conference.
“Having said that, the President really needs CIF,” he added.
The Office of the President’s P4.5 billion proposed CIF for 2027 is the same level as this year.
Of the P4.5 billion, P2.25 billion accounts for confidential funds while another P2.25 billion is for intelligence funds.

The 2015 Joint Circular governing the use of CIF defines confidential expenses as those expenses pertaining/related to surveillance activities in civilian government agencies that are intended to support the mandate or operations of the agency.

The same 2015 guidelines, on the other hand, define intelligence expenses as those related to intelligence information gathering activities of uniformed and military personnel, and intelligence practitioners that have a direct impact on national security.
Overall, the Marcos administration proposed a P10.77 billion worth of CIF for 2027, down from this year’s P11.8 billion allocation.
Of the proposed amount, P4.368 billion is for confidential funds and P6.405 billion for intelligence funds.
Abante, however, noted that such CIF must be properly accounted for.
Deputy Speaker and La Union Rep. Paolo Ortega V agreed.
“Importante kung merong nailaan o naibigay na pondo, dapat tama po ’yung paggamit, tama ’yung pinuntahan, at tama po ’yung proseso na sinusunod,” Ortega said.
(The fund should be used appropriately, meaning accountability process must be followed to the letter.)

Senate finance panel chairperson JV Ejercito earlier said that the CIF should be limited to agencies whose mandates involve law enforcement, intelligence and national security, and that the OP falls squarely within that justification.
Ejercito even said that the President, by the virtue of his position, will be subjected to threats.

One of the allegations of the House prosecution team in its impeachment case against Vice President Sara Duterte is alleged betrayal of public trust and culpable violation of the Constitution for apparently threatening to kill President Marcos, First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos and then-Speaker Ferdinand Martin Romualdez via a hitman if she herself was killed.
Abante, however, stressed that presidential confidential funds must still be properly used and accounted for.
“Kinakailangan po nating malaman lamang paano gagamitin ’yan, saan gagamitin ’yan,” he said.
(We need to know where these funds will be used for.)
Deputy Speaker and La Union Rep. Paolo Ortega V agreed, saying the key is ensuring that confidential funds are properly spent and established processes are followed.
(If there is an allocation for such, it is very important to ensure that it is disbursed appropriately and in accordance with accountability processes.)
Abolish CIF

But for opposition lawmaker Alliance of Concerned Teachers party-list Rep. Antonio Tinio of and Gabriela party-list Sarah Elago, the confidential fund spending of Vice President Sara Duterte which was marred with unusual recipient names should already prompt the abolition of the CIF allocation.

"That is why we have always called for the CIF abolition. The budget should not have confidential allocations. It should be transparent, and there are other ways to ensure that security concerns are addressed," Tinio said.

"Nobody should be exempted from accountability, especially the Office of the President. We should abolish CIF and realign the fund for basic services such as health, education, housing agriculture, among others," Elago added. —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: Could Ford's fight with Trump swing key byelections to the PCs? Experts weigh in
articles.summary: After months on his political backfoot, Doug Ford was on the offensive this week, squaring off with Donald Trump in a war of words. Political analysts and experts say the fight plays to the premier's…

image.caption: Premier Doug Ford speaks at a news conference in Hamilton last Monday. During the event, Ford slammed Donald Trump, responding to insults from the U.S. president that day. (Evan Mitsui/CBC)

blocks.text: Toronto·Analysis

After months on his political backfoot, Doug Ford was on the offensive this week, squaring off with Donald Trump in a war of words. Political analysts and experts say the fight plays to the premier's strengths and has contributed to a spike in his approvals just ahead of three provincial key byelections this week.
Bump in Ford approvals could help Tories gain ground in close races
After months on his political backfoot, Doug Ford was on the offensive this week, squaring off with Donald Trump in a war of words.

Political analysts and experts say the fight with the mercurial U.S. president plays to the premier's strengths and has contributed to a spike in his approvals just ahead of three key provincial byelections this week.

Ford traded insults with Trump earlier this week after trade talks between American and Canadian negotiators broke down. On Monday, Trump compared the premier to his late brother, former Toronto mayor Rob Ford, calling him less charismatic, intelligent and impressive. He also labeled him a “flunky” of Prime Minister Mark Carney.
Ford swung back, blasting Trump as the “king of bankruptcies” and a “bully.”
“I've been in this game a lot longer than he has, I got skin on me like an alligator, and you think an insult from him hurts me?” Ford reacted.
Ford, Trump exchange insults over collapsed trade talks
Past fights with Trump a political boon for Ford

But being in conflict with Trump has been a winning formula for the premier. It helped him cruise to a third straight majority government win during the snap election in early 2025. This week, his personal approvals jumped by 12 points and his PCs moved into the lead in a Liaison Strategies opinion survey, taken on the same day he sparred with the president.
On Thursday, voters in Scarborough Southwest, York-Simcoe and Hamilton East–Stoney Creek will go to the polls to select new MPPs.

items: Ford, PC approval ratings go up days after war of words with Trump
Ford doubles down on 'kiss my ass' comment to Trump amid Canada-U.S. trade war

blocks.text: York-Simcoe, north of Toronto, has been a Tory stronghold since the district was created in 2007. The PCs have never won the riding with less than 40 per cent of the vote in the past six elections.
But the battles in both Scarborough Southwest and Hamilton East-Stoney Creek are believed to be close, and experts say Ford’s fight with Trump could drive up support for the PCs.

“I think it will help immeasurably,” said former Liberal cabinet minister John Milloy. “(Voters) are going to look at that ballot and the person who's most associated with the anti-Trump sentiment right now is Doug Ford. So this could help.”
'Ford desperately needed a channel changer': strategist

Milloy, who is now director of the Centre for Public Ethics at Martin Luther University College, said voter turnout for byelections is traditionally low. But Ford has tapped into simmering public anger at Trump and people are looking for outlets to vent that frustration.
Casting a ballot in the byelections could be one way to channel those emotions, Milloy said.
“I think it's very clever of him and I think it will motivate people to come out and vote, which is huge,” he said. “That's a big part of it. Just getting people to get off the couch.”

NDP strategist Erin Morrison said the Official Opposition has been hard at work in both Scarborough and Hamilton in an effort to win those byelections. The PCs have been mired in a series of controversies for months, including the purchase and sale of a private jet, an expense scandal and allegedly spying on a former opposition leader while she was on vacation.

“Ford desperately needed a channel changer — and the fact that he got one called Trump may help him in Hamilton East—Stoney Creek and Scarborough South West,” said Morrison, a vice-president at Texture Communications.
She believes the NDP are leading in both ridings, but will now have to work hard to get their vote out.
Fight with Trump plays to Ford's strengths; Duncan says

Conservative strategist Sam Duncan said the fight with Trump plays to the premier’s strengths. And his actions and rhetoric over the last week have reminded voters why they sent him back to to Queen’s Park with another majority government, he said.

“It's always been a strength of (Ford’s) to really understand how people are feeling, and I think he has met the moment emotionally where Ontarians and a lot of Canadians, frankly, feel from a rhetoric standpoint,” he said.

Duncan, who is a vice-president with Wellington Advocacy, said he doesn’t think Ford’s fight with Trump will help in the Scarborough byelection because he sees that as a race between the Liberals and NDP.
But in Hamilton, where the Tories took the riding from the New Democrats in 2022, it could make a difference, he said.
“Before this week I would have said it was going to be a toss-up but now I believe it is going to be solidly PC,” he said.

McMaster University political science professor Peter Graefe said the war of words with Trump could help improve the perception of Ford’s government overall, and that should bolster the PCs' vote share in the byelections. But he cautions against over-estimating the impact of the fight.

“In a place like Hamilton East, where the steel tariffs are of particular concern, his promises to protect the province may resonate a bit more,” he said. “But overall, I think the impact will be relatively marginal.”
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Shawn Jeffords is a Provincial Affairs Reporter covering Queen's Park for CBC Toronto. He has previously covered Toronto City Hall for CBC and the Ontario Legislature for The Canadian Press. You can reach him by emailing shawn.jeffords@cbc.ca.

articles.title: Corals in decline globally, nearly half a century of data shows
articles.summary: New research highlights the declines in living corals in reefs around the world, showing the unprecedented twin-danger of human-caused climate change and an expected record El Niño.

image.caption: The painstaking work of underwater surveys, seen here in southern Thailand in 2024, is helping catalog the declines in hard coral cover around the world. Data shows the 'window of recovery' for reefs is getting shorter, says lead author Manuel González Rivero. (Lillian Swuanrumpha/AFP/Getty Images)

blocks.text: The proportion of the world's reefs with living, stony stalks of hard corals is down significantly, according to a new global report on these vital ecosystems.

And as these reefs stare down a potentially record-breaking El Niño peak just months away, new research suggests the naturally-occurring warming phenomenon might be more intense than it used to be — a trend captured in coral skeletons.

The Status of Coral Reefs of the World 2025 says marine heatwaves and global bleaching events have taken a repetitive toll on the world's corals. This climate change-fuelled heat stress has driven hard coral coverage globally to roughly 25 per cent.

"Coral cover around the world used to be above 30 or 40 per cent back in the '80s," said Manuel González Rivero, lead author with the Australian Institute of Marine Science and global co-ordinator of the Global Coral Reef Monitoring Network.

But he adds that the main takeaway is "not only that we're seeing a loss in coral cover, but that the window of recovery is getting shorter and shorter," given extreme ocean heat events have been occurring more frequently.
Which is why the rate of recent coral cover decline relative to previous decades is also worrying at 9.5 per cent.

"This decline … is showing that we're losing big chunks of coral from the majority of the world's coral reefs — and it's associated with climate change,” said Emily Darling, director of Coral Reefs at the Wildlife Conservation Society, who was not involved in the report.
Windows closing

This status report is the seventh by the Global Coral Reef Monitoring Network, using data from close to 37,000 reef sites. Hard coral cover shows a clear downward trend of loss and recovery stretching back to 1980.
The declines, notably, come after a global bleaching event, or GBE — where hotter ocean temperatures cause corals to expel the symbiotic microscopic algae inside, turning them a ghostly white.

While bleaching itself is not a death sentence, it leaves the corals weak and susceptible to disease and death, starting a domino effect for all the microorganisms and larger marine species that depend on them as a source of food and shelter.
Corals can recover, if given time. However, of the four recorded GBEs, three have happened in just the last 15 years — with the latest only recently declared over.

"Corals have had nine months, just over a year, to try to recover," said Darling, "and now they're facing down the strongest 'super' El Niño on record and the hottest ocean temperatures ever recorded."
The lack of a decent recovery window means even resilient species, which Darling's recent research focused on, are getting hit repeatedly.
Good news about coral reefs and their climate resilience
Uneven declines

Of the 10 regions monitored in this report, Rivero says, the declines are seen in four — Australia, the eastern Pacific, the Caribbean and the area from the Persian Gulf out to the Arabian Sea. Other regions are stable, if not growing.

Corals in growth areas, however, are not immune to the added heat of the oceans. As humans burn fossil fuels, oceans absorb 90 per cent of the excess heat trapped by those greenhouse gases, leading to more intense and frequent marine heatwaves.

In the western Indian Ocean, which saw a significant increase in coral cover, the report notes "data sparsity prior to 1998 and uneven monitoring efforts" can "limit the accuracy of estimates of hard coral cover," adding that it and other regions may have actually experienced a decline.

Darling says confidence in the data has improved, because the number of people doing the diving, measuring and counting has gone up. But she also echoes the report's call for sustained funding and standardizing monitoring methods in order to better understand the global picture of reefs.
"There's still hope for increasing resilience to coral reefs," Darling said, but warned that ocean temperatures are getting hotter.
"And we are slowly boiling corals to death."
LISTEN | Repetitive strain on our oceans:
Quirks and Quarks15:12Climate change is making marine heat waves more frequent and intense – and that's changing life in the ocean
Action on a global and regional level

While the report's data brings the decline of corals into focus, the calls to action are also clear. Given reefs support an estimated 25 per cent of marine life and contribute to the economy and coastal protection of more than 100 countries, the authors advocate for global and local action.

On a regional level, "second-stage interventions" such as limiting overfishing, pollution and coastal development can "increase the resilience of coral reefs and their likelihood of surviving and recovering from extreme events," according to the report.
But on a global level, Rivero says, we need to stop emitting greenhouse gases by burning fossil fuels.

"Climate change is driving the warming of the oceans and that warming of oceans is driving the decline that we've seen on coral reefs. There's no doubt about it," Rivero told CBC News from Townsville, Australia.
El Niño may be getting worse

The current danger is more heat ahead with El Niño gaining strength on top of a baseline raised by climate change. But new research published in Science says recent El Niño events have been stronger — and corals themselves are a calendar of proof.

"Corals can live for decades to centuries, and in the chemistry of their skeleton, they preserve a history of the conditions that they grow under," said Julia Cole, paleoclimatologist and chair of the department of earth and environmental sciences at the University of Michigan.
"In warm conditions, corals are building their skeleton with a different chemistry than during cold conditions."

items: Oceans dangerously acidic from carbon emissions, report warns
El Niño is here, and it’s already looking like it could be 'mind-blowing'

blocks.text: By studying the geochemistry of corals in the Galápagos — what Cole refers to as the heart of El Niño country — the study was able to go effectively back in time. It found evidence of stronger El Niño events in the last 40 years compared to a time before 1850.

Cole cautions that El Niño is complex and this is not predictive of future events, but there is a shift in the last few decades as the world has gotten warmer from the burning of fossil fuels. For corals, that's not good news.
"It really adds to this urgency and also a deep concern.... If this is where we are now, where are we going in the next 10 years?" Darling told CBC News.
"Because we know that a lot of this warming is committed and even if we turn things around today we still have a ways to go before the ecological systems on our planet start to respond to that."

articles.title: Hundreds march through Bulacan floods in protest vs corruption
articles.summary: Floodwaters have become the protest ground for angry Bulacan residents.

blocks.text: Groups march in flooded Bulacan to protest against the anomalous flood control projects and coastal reclamation on Aug. 31, 2026.
Pamalakaya

MANILA, Philippines — Hundreds of residents, farmers and fisherfolk waded through flooded roads in Bulacan on Monday, August 31, to protest corruption in flood-control projects and reclamation developments that they blame for worsening the province's chronic flooding.

The National Heroes Day protest was led by the anti-corruption alliance Kilos Bulacan, with members of fisherfolk group Pamalakaya, farmers' group Kilusang Magbubukid ng Pilipinas and Anakpawis Party-list joining the march in Malolos.
The groups said extreme weather triggered the recent downpours but argued that flawed flood-control projects and environmental destruction have magnified their impact.

"Napapanahon ang inilunsad na protesta ng mga residente, magsasaka, at mangingisda sa Bulacan para muling manawagan ng hustisya at pananagutan sa lahat ng sangkot sa maanomalya at palpak na flood control, ganundin sa malaganap na pandarambong ng kalikasan na nagpapalubog ng mga komunidad," Pamalakaya Vice Chairperson Ronnel Arambulo said.

("The protest by residents, farmers and fisherfolk in Bulacan comes at a crucial time to again demand justice and accountability from all those involved in anomalous and failed flood-control projects, as well as widespread environmental destruction that is submerging communities.")
Pamalakaya also pointed to the 2,500-hectare New Manila International Airport development in Bulakan town, which involves reclamation along the Manila Bay coast.
The group claimed the project has displaced nearly 1,000 fishing families in Barangay Taliptip and resulted in the removal of more than 600 mangrove trees.
KMP chairperson Danilo Ramos, a Malolos resident, said farmers continue to suffer losses from repeated flooding.

"Farmers and residents of Bulacan have long endured the repeated flooding caused by these useless, anomalous flood-control projects. While corrupt officials and big corporations plunder the public funds and our environment, ordinary people suffer," Ramos said.
"We demand justice in the form of genuine mitigation measures, accountability, and appropriate compensation for this systematic disaster that caused unmeasurable losses," he added.
Bulacan has remained heavily flooded after successive tropical cyclones and days of southwest monsoon, or habagat, rains. The province is under a state of calamity.
Mass in the floods
Floodwaters have also reached historic Barasoain Church in Malolos, where parish activities continued despite the inundation.
Photos posted by the Our Lady of Mount Carmel Parish showed people attending Mass and baptisms and holding funeral Masses despite floodwaters around parts of the church.
The church was already inundated Sunday as persistent habagat rains soaked Bulacan.

articles.title: Weather tracker: Warm Yellow Sea strengthens storms in South Korea
articles.summary:
More than 200mm of rain forecast in parts of South Korea, while parts of southern Europe to be 10C above average

South Korea’s prime minister, Han Seong-sook, met officials to prepare for…

blocks.text: South Korea’s prime minister, Han Seong-sook, met officials to prepare for heavy rain expected this week, with rainfall totals across central and northern parts of the country forecast to exceed 200mm in some areas.

South Korea was battered by heavy rainfall earlier this month and some areas were particularly hard hit. Over the weekend further thunderstorms pushed into the region and these are expected to cause disruption through Monday. This heavy rain is caused by a series of severe thunderstorms that developed over the Yellow Sea, on the western side of South Korea, and will slowly push eastwards on Monday before easing on Tuesday. These storms have been strengthened by the very warm Yellow Sea, which now has a surface temperature of 29C, 4C above the climatological average.

Thailand is also under a warning for heavy to very heavy rain as the country passes the middle of its monsoon season, which runs from May to October. In the Philippines, the province of Tarlac has been placed under a state of calamity due to prolonged heavy rain in August.

Nearby in the north Pacific, which has had an active typhoon and tropical storm season so far and will continue to do so this week, several tropical systems have the potential to develop. Last week, Typhoon Bang-lang and Tropical Storm Etau developed very close to each other in the north-west Pacific and both travelled northwards, although neither made landfall. Another two systems near the Philippines and China have a medium to high chance of developing into a tropical cyclone. For this to happen, wind speeds need to reach 39mph (63km/h). Across in the eastern north Pacific, Karina has developed into a category 1 hurricane and is expected to head just to the north of Hawaii but is not forecast to make landfall. Tropical Storm Lowell is expected to strengthen into a hurricane on Tuesday before passing just to the south of Hawaii.

As Europe reaches the end of its record-breaking meteorological summer, the hot weather is showing no signs of easing off for the start of September. The heat is expected to intensify again later this week across central and southern parts of Europe, with temperatures rising to 10C above the climatological average. In Bosnia and Herzegovina, temperatures could reach about 40C by the weekend, falling just shy of the country’s all-time temperature record of 43.1C, set in 2007.

articles.title: DSWD releases 2.3 million food packs to families hit by floods, landslides
articles.summary: The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) has released about 2.3 million family food packs to families affected by successive storms and flooding, while maintaining millions more in…

blocks.text: The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) has released about 2.3 million family food packs to families affected by successive storms and flooding, while maintaining millions more in reserve as the southwest monsoon or “habagat” continues to affect parts of the country.
DSWD Secretary Rex Gatchalian said the 2.3 million food packs released over the past several weeks represent one of the largest relief distributions in the agency’s history.
“That is one of the largest releases of family food packs in our history because we are talking about almost four weeks and 2.3 million food packs,” he added.
Gatchalian said the DSWD would continue distributing and replenishing its relief supplies as more communities deal with the effects of recent weather disturbances.
DSWD currently has 3,586,913 family food packs, 301,570 ready-to-eat food packs, and 282,931 non-food items prepositioned in strategic locations nationwide.

The relief supplies are being used to augment assistance for communities affected by Tropical Cyclones Luis, Maymay, and Neneng, as well as recent flooding in Central Luzon and parts of the National Capital Region (NCR).
DSWD field offices remain in coordination with local government units (LGUs) to monitor weather developments, assess emergency situations, and respond to requests for additional relief supplies.
“The ones distributing to the beneficiaries or victims are the local government units because, remember, they are the first responders. We only provide augmentation,” Gatchalian said.

“As far as we know, we have complied with all the requests we have received from local government units. But some local government units are already asking for a second or third round, and rightfully so, because this disaster has gone on for quite some time,” he added.
Repacking hubs and supply chains nationwide continue to operate to replenish prepositioned relief supplies and ensure that resources remain available for communities affected by disasters.

articles.summary: ZAMBOANGA CITY- Zamboanga city joined the nation in commemorating National Heroes’ Day through a program held at Plaza Rizal on Monday, August 31. The program, which started with a flag raising…

blocks.text: (Photo courtesy of Zamboanga City PIO)
ZAMBOANGA CITY- Zamboanga city joined the nation in commemorating National Heroes’ Day through a program held at Plaza Rizal on Monday, August 31.

The program, which started with a flag raising ceremony, was participated in by officials and members of the security sector, government officials and personnel, Boy Scouts of the Philippines and academic institutions.
During the program, officials honored both historic and modern day heroes as both offer their lives in service to the public.
Mayor Khymer Olaso honored historical heroes and said that their heroism lives on through the modern heroes of today.
"The true meaning of heroism is the willingness to serve others without expecting anything in return. We must do more for our city and continue to rise above every challenge, "Olaso said.

Meanwhile, WestMinCom Deputy Commander BGen. Bayani Curaming, Deputy Commander for Internal Defense Operations said that heroism and courage from our national heroes continue to live on in the present time.
Curaming lauded active-duty members in the security sector and civil servants who risk personal comfort to serve the public.
"Let us show the nation that bravery born in August 1896 lives on in Zamboanga City," Curaming urged.

articles.title: Don’t be afraid to LARP
articles.summary: By Nicolette David 4th-year BFA Creative Writing student Ateneo de Manila University I recently traveled to Singapore with one of my girlfriends, and there was one Gen Z slang term we couldn’t stop…

blocks.text: By Nicolette David
4th-year BFA Creative Writing student
Ateneo de Manila University

I recently traveled to Singapore with one of my girlfriends, and there was one Gen Z slang term we couldn’t stop saying: “LARPing.” We either called ourselves “LARPers” or our actions as larping, because everything we did on that short weekend vacation was exactly that.

We posted Instagram stories a day or two late to make it appear as if we’d been there longer, dressed up to eat at a fancy restaurant that dented the bank, and paid almost ₱2,000 for access to the ever-so bougie Marina Bay Sands’ rooftop bar, Cé La Vi, to take photos of the city from way up above and pretend we’re hotel guests, even though we stayed somewhere three times cheaper. Basically, we were LARPing.
What is larping?

The term LARP or LARPing comes from “live-action role-play,” a type of role-playing game in which participants play fictional characters in real-life. Nowadays, LARPing, like its earlier meaning, refers to acting out a certain role in real life, essentially faking expertise or identity. It is now used in the same way that we call someone a “tryhard” or “performative.”

In meme culture, LARP or LARPing is commonly used to mock people who flaunt a luxurious lifestyle that they do not actually own or can maintain. Gen Z is quick to judge people who create the illusion of financial success, particularly on social media, such as renting luxury items ranging from sports cars to designer bags or staying in expensive hotel lobbies or stores just to shoot dozens of photos and videos to post over a couple of weeks.

Staging a high-luxury lifestyle is, without a doubt, a hardcore LARP. However, few people realize that there are smaller, perhaps unnoticeable, ways people LARP daily, especially if we go back to the term’s original meaning as performance. To LARP is to perform, but haven’t we been doing that already?
Daily LARPs

Take a look at popular aesthetics online, such as “clean girl,” “quiet luxury,” and so on. Many adopt an aesthetic archetype and put in the effort to showcase that lifestyle. People post online about their expensive workout classes or elegant clothing pieces, depending on what they want to be perceived as. We dress, eat, and live in a way that we want to embody.

Another example of daily LARPing occurs in a workplace environment, where we can essentially fake expertise. I’m not talking about outright fraud, but rather faking confidence by sharing your opinions even if you’re shy or using workplace jargon to make people feel like you fit right in the job; but as we fake confidence, we can reduce the anxiety we may feel within.

A form of LARPing that many already do is social media content staging. For instance, posting in upscale eateries or cafes, curating a photo dump to showcase only the cool, effortless-looking moments, releasing vacation photos days later to give the impression that you were there longer, posting in the gym like you’re an expert even if you’ve just started, or editing certain parts of a photo to highlight the best features of yourself. Like a vision board, you project a lifestyle that you might not have fully attained in real life.

All of these small everyday self-conscious habits involve curating oneself to fit into a specific demographic. It may not be intentional, but it’s still a performance, and you could’ve just been LARPing this entire time.
To LARP or not to LARP?

But don’t start deleting all your social media posts or crying to your boss that you’re a fraud; there is nothing wrong with LARPing. As author James Pack said, “Life is a performance. Earn an ovation.” So, yes, the world’s a stage, but with that you can act with purpose because LARPing can go deeper than copying a chosen identity. Rather than simply focusing on how others perceive you, the motivation to embody a potential self can slowly but surely become more and more genuine.

As the common saying goes, “fake it till you make it,” and if LARPing has the power to give you confidence to allow yourself to learn through performing as though you’ve already achieved your goals, then, as Gen Z may say: “Chat, I think I’ve found the method.”
When you behave like the person you want to be and push through the unknown, you gradually let go of self-doubt and angst. Then, LARPing becomes a step toward becoming your best self.

This is why I’m not ashamed to call myself a LARPer. I’ll walk into a steakhouse as if I belong there or into a luxury store only to try on items and add them to my future wishlist. At work, I’ll proudly state that I’m a confident person and use workplace jargon that I may or may not have just researched online. Funny enough, what started as a slang term, LARPing, motivates me to work harder, learn more, and face my fears because I can envision the life I want to achieve.
Perhaps, when done right, LARPing is the way to bring out one’s courage to try and turn their dreams into reality?

“Voices” is Manila Bulletin Lifestyle’s dedicated space for young writers and future journalists to speak up about the topics that matter to their generation—from pop culture and social trends to education, and everything in between.

articles.title: 5 uncommon botanicals and functional foods
articles.summary: Are you taking multivitamins, omega-3 fish oil, herbal supplements, and the like? These products fall under a broad group of natural health products commonly known as dietary or food supplements.…

blocks.text: Are you taking multivitamins, omega-3 fish oil, herbal supplements, and the like? These products fall under a broad group of natural health products commonly known as dietary or food supplements.

Marketing of food supplements, nutraceuticals, and other similar products has grown tremendously. This is primarily due to the increase in awareness of their advantages in preventive health. More people are also becoming inclined to adopt natural and alternative approaches due to the increasing cost of pharmaceuticals or medicines, as well as their negative side effects.

According to Fortune Business Insights, the global nutraceuticals market size was valued at $547.68 billion in 2026 and is estimated to grow to $1,124.56 billion by the year 2034. That is more than double the increase in just eight years. Consumers, however, must be vigilant and not just fall prey to false marketing claims. Neither should a patient randomly take any nutraceutical product without the guidance of a registered nutritionist-dietitian and physician.

According to the Implementing Rules and Regulations of the Nutrition and Dietetics Law of 2016, RA 10862, registered nutritionist-dietitians lawfully provide quality food and nutrition products, programs, and services aimed at optimizing the health and well-being of clients. Therefore, be wary of fake nutritionists and health coaches who recommend supplementation without the clinical background and professional license required by Philippine law. You may purchase nutraceutical products from laypeople, but always do so after consulting a Registered Nutritionist-Dietitian for proper guidance.

It is important to understand the differences among various dietary supplements. These products may belong under one group for legal and commercial purposes, but they were created differently for various purposes and health benefits.

Nutraceuticals are isolated bioactive compounds from food that provide medical and health benefits. An example would be the omega-3 found in fatty fish and resveratrol that is isolated and concentrated from plant foods that contain polyphenols, such as black grapes.

Dietary supplements are concentrated, usually synthetic sources of nutrients such as vitamins, minerals, amino acids, enzymes, etc., that provide specific nutrients to correct deficiencies or bridge the nutrition gap when food intake is inadequate. An example is ferrous sulfate for iron deficiency anemia and ketoanalogues prescribed to kidney patients on a very low-protein diet.

Botanicals are plants or parts of plants, such as leaves, flowers, bark, roots, seeds, or fruits, that have functional health benefits. Examples are turmeric root, ginger root, ginkgo biloba, and aloe vera.

Functional foods are food or food ingredients that have additional health or physiological benefits beyond the normal nutritional values they provide (calories, carbohydrates, protein, and fat). Functional foods provide phytochemicals or plant nutrients, fiber, and antioxidants from plant food sources in wholesome form. When they are processed into liquid, freeze-dried, powdered, or pill form for convenience, they are known as modified functional foods.
The Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics, formerly known as the American Dietetic Association, issued a position statement on functional foods:

“All foods are functional at some physiological level, but it is the position of the American Dietetic Association (ADA) that functional foods that include whole foods and fortified, enriched, or enhanced foods have a potentially beneficial effect on health when consumed as part of a varied diet on a regular basis, at effective levels. The ADA supports research to further define the health benefits and risks of individual functional foods and their physiologically active components. Health claims on food products, including functional foods, should be based on the significant scientific agreement standard of evidence, and the ADA supports label claims based on such strong scientific substantiation. Food and nutrition professionals will continue to work with the food industry, allied health professionals, the government, the scientific community, and the media to ensure that the public has accurate information regarding functional foods and thus should continue to educate themselves on this emerging area of food and nutrition science.”
Here are some uncommon botanicals and functional foods and their health benefits:
Cordyceps sinensis and mycelium

This mushroom contains polysaccharides (carbohydrates) that stimulate the immune system by increasing the production of natural killer cells to fight cancer cells and infections. It contains lectins that recognize and scavenge cancer cells. It also helps protect the kidneys and liver. Studies have shown that among post-kidney transplant patients, the phytonutrient cordycepin found in these mushrooms is associated with improvement in graft function, anemia, and leukopenia, and synergistically suppresses organ rejection by reducing drug-induced side effects.
American ginseng

This is different from Korean or Asian ginseng. American ginseng contains adaptogenic properties for stress, thereby enhancing sleep and promoting heart health. It helps with blood glucose regulation, immune regulation, and nerve regeneration. The phytonutrient ginsenosides also helps inhibit tumor formation.
Hawthorn

It is very rich in nitric oxide, which helps with heart health by regulating blood pressure, cholesterol, and triglycerides. It enhances blood circulation and sleep quality. Hawthorn has protective properties for the kidneys by reducing oxidative stress.
Opuntia cactus

Also known as prickly pear cactus, this plant has antioxidant activity that is seven times higher than the supplement vitamin C. It has 10,000 phytochemicals and antioxidants that increase the activity of the immune system’s natural killer cells. This plant reduces oxidative damage to the kidneys and liver, provides relief from digestive problems by coating the intestinal and stomach lining, and aids with blood glucose regulation and collagen formation. Therefore, it enhances skin integrity and lubricates the joints.
Mangosteen pericarp

The peel of the mangosteen has around 40 types of phytonutrients, xanthones. It acts as a natural anti-allergy by preventing the production of histamine in mast cells (immune cells). The peel cannot be eaten raw; that is why it is processed and taken in powdered or pill form.
Berberine

The bark and root of this shrub aid in regulating blood glucose, cholesterol, and triglycerides. It also has anti-inflammatory, antifungal, and antimicrobial properties. The phytochemicals in berberine trigger activated protein kinase, which improves the body’s metabolism. This plant promotes liver and gut health.
When it comes to your health, don’t take chances. Let a health professional take care of you. Consult a health professional before purchasing and consuming any health product.

articles.title: Baguio records two deaths out of 585 dengue cases
articles.summary: BAGUIO CITY—The City Health Services Office reported two deaths from dengue, among the 585 dengue cases recorded from January 1 to August 15, lower than the 698 cases recorded during the same period…

blocks.text: (Pixabay)

BAGUIO CITY—The City Health Services Office reported two deaths from dengue, among the 585 dengue cases recorded from January 1 to August 15, lower than the 698 cases recorded during the same period last year.
The two suspected dengue deaths involved a 31-year-old man and a 25-year-old man.
With this, the CHSO urged residents to remain vigilant against dengue fever as the ongoing rains could create additional mosquito breeding grounds.
City Health Officer Dr. Celia Flor Brillantes said dengue cases in the city remain below the city’s epidemic threshold despite an observed increase at the end of July.
She warned that rainwater can accumulate in both natural and artificial containers, creating more potential breeding grounds for mosquitoes.
Residents are encouraged to regularly inspect their homes and surroundings and remove stagnant water from containers, discarded items, garbage and other areas where rainwater can accumulate.
According to the City Epidemiology and Surveillance Unit, dengue cases in the city have decreased by 16 percent this year.
The analysis showed that the spread of dengue remains localized, with cases reported in 73 barangays during the four-week monitoring period.
The CHSO continues to implement dengue prevention measures, including community clean-up drives, case investigations and information campaigns promoting the 5S strategy against dengue.

articles.title: Whirlwind damages 10 houses in Ilocos Sur
articles.summary: VIGAN CITY, Ilocos Sur — At least 10 houses were partially damaged after a strong whirlwind swept through two villages in Burgos, Ilocos Sur, on Sunday evening, August 30. Ilocos Sur Provincial…

blocks.text: VIGAN CITY, Ilocos Sur — At least 10 houses were partially damaged after a strong whirlwind swept through two villages in Burgos, Ilocos Sur, on Sunday evening, August 30.

Ilocos Sur Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Officer Rhon Arquelada said the incident occurred at around 6 p.m. at the height of heavy rains brought by the enhanced southwest monsoon, or Habagat.
No injuries were reported.
The whirlwind struck Barangays Manaboc and Bangbangar, damaging the roofs of several houses and some garages and uprooting trees due to strong winds.

According to the Burgos Municipal Police Station, barangay officials alerted authorities about the whirlwind while police were conducting situational monitoring in the municipality through handheld radios.
Police personnel and members of the Municipal Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office immediately responded to verify the reports and assess the damage.
Authorities assisted affected residents and helped move them to safer areas while clearing operations were conducted in the affected communities.
Arquelada said the Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office remains on heightened alert as heavy rains associated with the Habagat continue to affect the province.
As of 11 a.m. Sunday, at least 52 families from 15 towns in Ilocos Sur remained in evacuation centers for their safety amid the continuing heavy rains, he said.

articles.title: 33 dead, 19 injured, 3 missing amid cyclones, ‘habagat’—OCD
articles.summary: Thirty-three people died, 19 were injured, and three remained missing amid the effects of Tropical Cyclones “Luis,” “Maymay,” and “Neneng” and the southwest monsoon, or “habagat,” the Office of Civil…

blocks.text: (PCG PHOTO)

Thirty-three people died, 19 were injured, and three remained missing amid the effects of Tropical Cyclones “Luis,” “Maymay,” and “Neneng” and the southwest monsoon, or “habagat,” the Office of Civil Defense (OCD) reported on Monday, Aug. 31.
OCD Disaster Preparedness Service Director Vicente Gregorio Tomas said during the briefing that the figures were recorded as of noon.
“Ang mga namatay po, 33 po ang naka-record. Injured is 19. Missing naman po is tatlo (There were 33 recorded deaths, 19 injured persons, and three missing persons),” he said.
Tomas added that 2.5 million families, comprising 8.8 million individuals, were affected by the weather disturbances.

blocks.caption: (PCG PHOTO)

blocks.text: He identified Regions I, II, III, V, VI, IX, Calabarzon, the Cordillera Administrative Region, National Capital Region, and Mimaropa among the affected areas.
According to OCD, a total of 1,365 evacuation centers were accommodating 46,900 families, or 164,500 individuals.

“Number of evacuation centers totals to 1,365. Ang families po inside the different evacuation centers is 46,900, and individuals po is 164,500 (The number of evacuation centers totals 1,365. There are 46,900 families, or 164,500 individuals, inside the different evacuation centers),” Tomas said.
As such, the OCD official reported that 3,300 houses were damaged, with 2,900 partially damaged and 405 totally damaged.

blocks.caption: (PCG PHOTO)

blocks.text: “Sa damages naman po ay houses, 3,300; ang partially po doon ay 2,900; ang totally damaged naman po ay 405 (As for housing damage, 3,300 houses were affected; 2,900 were partially damaged, while 405 were totally damaged),” he said.
OCD said damage to infrastructure reached ₱6.12 billion, while agricultural damage stood at ₱2.32 billion.
According to Tomas, assistance provided to affected communities totaled ₱1.78 billion, while 117 areas were under a state of calamity.

“As regards sa assistance provided po, in total po P1.78 billion, and of course the state of calamity is in 117 areas (Assistance provided totaled ₱1.78 billion, while 117 areas are under a state of calamity),” he said.

articles.title: QC gov’t to penalize projects that leave construction debris
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Infrastructure projects in Quezon City that leave construction debris, waste or damaged public facilities behind could face penalties and delays in project acceptance under a…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Infrastructure projects in Quezon City that leave construction debris, waste or damaged public facilities behind could face penalties and delays in project acceptance under a new city ordinance.

The Quezon City government said all public and private infrastructure projects must secure a Certificate of Site Restoration and Cleanup Compliance (CSRCC) before they can be officially accepted or fully authorized under the Quezon City Construction Site Restoration and Cleanup Compliance Ordinance (SP-3519, S-2026).

The ordinance seeks to prevent construction debris from blocking roads, sidewalks, drainage systems, waterways and other public spaces, which the city government said could worsen flooding and endanger residents.

“Every infrastructure project must be completed in a safe, orderly, and environmentally responsible manner. No developer or project proponent should be allowed to leave behind debris that threatens our people, communities, and environment,” Mayor Joy Belmonte said.

Under the ordinance, project proponents must clear construction and demolition debris, restore affected roads, sidewalks, drainage systems and rights-of-way, and ensure proper backfilling and compaction.
They must also comply with engineering, environmental and waste-management regulations and ensure that debris is transported, disposed of, recovered or recycled only through authorized facilities.

The city government said the CSRCC will be issued only after the project secures the required clearances, including a Technical Restoration Clearance from the Quezon City Department of Engineering and an Environmental Compliance Inspection Report from the Department of Sanitation and Cleanup Works of Quezon City.

“The Department of Building Official will oversee privately owned or privately funded projects, while the Quezon City Department of Engineering will have jurisdiction over projects owned or funded by the City Government. District Action Offices and barangays will assist in monitoring and reporting noncompliant projects,” it added.

Violators may face monetary penalties and other sanctions, including withholding of project acceptance until the CSRCC is secured, suspension or denial of building-related permits, forfeiture or non-release of performance bonds or guarantees for public infrastructure projects, and suspension or closure of ongoing construction operations until compliance is achieved. /mr

articles.title: 320 kilos of undocumented meat products seized in Occidental Mindoro
articles.summary: CALAPAN CITY, Oriental Mindoro — Authorities seized 320 kilograms of cooked and uncooked processed meat products shipped from Metro Manila after receiving a tip from a concerned citizen in the…

blocks.text: CALAPAN CITY, Oriental Mindoro — Authorities seized 320 kilograms of cooked and uncooked processed meat products shipped from Metro Manila after receiving a tip from a concerned citizen in the Occidental Mindoro town of Mamburao on Aug. 29.

Municipal veterinarian Dr. Nathaniel Descanzo said the shipment failed to meet documentary and transport requirements under Executive Order No. 32, Series of 2026, issued by Mayor Glicerio Almero III on July 20.
The order strengthened an earlier directive issued by Occidental Mindoro Gov. Eduardo Gadiano regulating the entry and movement of meat products in the municipality.

The 17 boxes of meat products were intercepted by the joint team of the Mamburao Municipal Police Station and the Municipal Veterinary Office after they were reportedly unloaded from a trucking service, according to the Mamburao Public Information Office in a post on Monday (August 31).

Among the documents required for meat shipments are the Food and Drug Administration license to operate and certificate of product registration of the manufacturer or distributor, veterinary shipping permit, meat transport vehicle accreditation and license, and a letter of acceptance from the municipal veterinarian’s office.
Meat shipments must also undergo prescribed inspection and unloading procedures.

Authorities may confiscate meat products that are transported without the required documents, are improperly handled or refrigerated, or are accompanied by falsified or altered papers, according to the municipal veterinary office.
The stricter enforcement is also aimed at preventing the spread of African swine fever (ASF), a viral disease that affects pigs but does not infect humans.
Contaminated pork and pork products can contribute to the spread of ASF, potentially causing deaths among hogs and losses to raisers, as well as disrupting local pork supplies and pushing up prices.

Authorities also warned that undocumented and uninspected meat products could pose food safety risks, including bacterial contamination and foodborne illnesses, particularly when the cold chain is broken or proper handling and temperature requirements are not followed.
The municipal government urged meat traders, trucking companies and online sellers to comply with regulations governing the transport and sale of meat products. /mr

blocks.text: SAN ANTONIO, Zambales — The developer of a project inside the Subic Bay Freeport said it would submit to full transparency and accountability as authorities investigate a landslide that killed two workers and injured two others over the weekend.

In a statement on Monday (Aug. 31), Xantheng (Subic) International Corp. (XSIC), the management arm of the Tipo Hightech Eco Park, said it immediately responded and coordinated with the Subic Bay Metropolitan Authority (SBMA) and other relevant agencies for site assessment, verification and appropriate measures.
An Aug. 29 erosion along Tipo Road had killed a Chinese employee and a Filipino worker, after they were caught by the moving soil. Two others were injured.

XSIC referred to the incident as a “soil erosion incident” and said it occurred following prolonged periods of heavy rainfall throughout August in the Subic Bay Freeport Zone, surrounding areas and Central Luzon.
“This cooperation also extends to investigation of the incident to establish the facts, conditions, and other circumstances surrounding this unfortunate event,” the company said.
XSIC said it was communicating with the affected persons and families and extending necessary assistance.
It also said it was closely monitoring the affected area, including prevailing weather and ground conditions, while undertaking precautionary measures in coordination with authorities.
“We recognize the concerns arising from this incident and remain committed to addressing the matter with due diligence, transparency, and accountability,” XSIC said.
SBMA earlier said it was investigating the incident and coordinating with the concerned parties to determine the circumstances surrounding the landslide. /mr

articles.title: Suspect in MSU-Marawi Catholic Mass bombing killed – military
articles.summary: ILIGAN CITY, Lanao del Norte — A suspect in the Dec. 3, 2023, bombing inside the Mindanao State University (MSU) campus in Marawi City was killed along with his wife last Saturday evening, the…

blocks.text: ILIGAN CITY, Lanao del Norte — A suspect in the Dec. 3, 2023, bombing inside the Mindanao State University (MSU) campus in Marawi City was killed along with his wife last Saturday evening, the military said on Monday.

Four people were killed and 50 others were wounded when the bomb exploded while Catholics were celebrating Mass inside the campus gymnasium. The attack was blamed on the Islamic State-aligned Dawlah Islamiyah-Maute Group (DI-Maute Group).

Maj. Candidato Paduman, civil-military operations officer of the 103rd Infantry “Haribon” Brigade (103IB), said joint government security forces killed Mohaimen Hadji, alias Ibn Sali/Usama, a DI-Maute Group member, and his wife, Nesren Camar Solaiman, alias “Nesren,” during an operation in Marawi City.

He said the two were killed while troops were serving warrants of arrest against Khadafi Mimbisa, alias “Engineer,” and Mohaimen Hadji for alleged violations of Republic Act 11479, or the Anti-Terrorism Act of 2022.
He said the troops were fired upon while approaching the targets, prompting them to retaliate.

Paduman said Mohaimen Hadji, purportedly the DI-Maute Group’s financial link to the Islamic State, allegedly fabricated and planted the improvised explosive device (IED) used in the MSU-Marawi campus attack.
Paduman confirmed that Mimbisa managed to escape, but a manhunt to arrest him continues.

Capt. Steffi Salanguit, spokesperson for the Police Regional Office of the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region (PROBAR), said on Sunday evening that a 6-month-old infant was also killed in the incident after a suspected grenade allegedly left by Mimbisa, also spelled Minbesa, exploded.
She said the joint law enforcement operation was launched around 11 p.m. in Barangay Tampilong, Marawi City, under “Oplan Pagtugis.”
Paduman said the operating team recovered an M16 rifle, a .45-caliber pistol and IED components at the encounter scene.

In a text message on Monday, Brig. Gen. Jerry Montoya, commander of the 1st Infantry “Tabak” Division (1ID), said the strength of the DI-Maute Group was further weakened by the slaying of Mohaimen Hadji.
He assured that the military would continue to go after the terrorist group and disband it.

The operation was led by the Lanao del Sur Police Provincial Office, with support from the 1403rd Regional Mobile Force Battalion, 1st Provincial Mobile Force Company, Provincial Intelligence Unit, Provincial Explosive Ordnance and Canine Unit, Task Force Marawi, Marawi City Police Station, and the Army’s 1st Infantry Division and 103rd Infantry Brigade. /mcm
