articles.title: You don’t need to be famous to be a hero--Speaker Dy
articles.summary: Individuals of renown don't have a monopoly on heroism, as even common Filipinos can be heroes. House Speaker Isabela 6th district Rep. Faustino "Bojie" Dy III had this to say Monday, Aug. 31 on the…

blocks.text: Individuals of renown don't have a monopoly on heroism, as even common Filipinos can be heroes.
House Speaker Isabela 6th district Rep. Faustino "Bojie" Dy III had this to say Monday, Aug. 31 on the occasion of National Heroes' Day.
Amid rapid changes in society and around the world, Dy said Filipinos should hold fast to enduring Filipino values that have long defined the nation and its heroes.

“Sa isang panahon na mabilis magbago ang mundo, kailangan nating bumalik sa mga pagpapahalagang hindi dapat magbago: katapatan sa salita at gawa, paggalang sa kapwa, malasakit sa nangangailangan, tapang na panindigan ang tama, at pagmamahal sa bayan,” he said.

(At a time when the world is changing rapidly, we need to return to the values that should never change: honesty in words and deeds, respect for others, compassion for those in need, the courage to stand up for what is right, and love of country.)
Dy added: "Ito ang tunay na mukha ng kabayanihan sa ating panahon.”
(This is the true face of heroism in our time.)
The Speaker emphasized that heroism wasn't reserved for famous figures or extraordinary acts; these be practiced by every Filipino through everyday acts of goodness and service.
“Hindi kailangang maging tanyag upang maging bayani. Hindi kailangang gumawa ng pambihira upang makapaglingkod,” he said.
(One does not have to be famous to be a hero. One does not have to do something extraordinary to serve.)
“Kailangan lamang nating piliing maging mabuting Pilipino—araw-araw, sa bawat pagkakataon," Dy said in a poignant reminder to his countrymen.
(We only need to choose to be good Filipinos—every day, at every opportunity.)
According to Dy, National Heroes Day should serve as both a remembrance of the past and a reminder of the responsibility of the present generation.
“Ang National Heroes Day ay hindi lamang araw ng paggunita. Ito ay araw ng pagpapaalala kung sino tayo bilang mga Pilipino,” Dy said.
(National Heroes Day is not only a day of remembrance. It is a day to remind us of who we are as Filipinos.)

“Ang ating mga bayani ay nag-iwan sa atin ng isang mahalagang pamana: ang paniniwalang may mga bagay na higit na mahalaga kaysa sa sarili—ang bayan, ang kapwa, at ang kinabukasan ng susunod na henerasyon.”
(Our heroes left us an important legacy: the belief that there are things more important than oneself—the country, our fellow Filipinos, and the future of the next generation.)
The Speaker said that responsibility now rests with today’s generation of Filipinos.

articles.title: Malacañang defends Marcos' honorary degree from PLM
articles.summary: Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Claire Castro on Monday hit back at those questioning the honorary Doctor of Laws degree recently conferred by the Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Maynila (PLM) on…

blocks.text: Published August 31, 2026 3:27pm

Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Claire Castro on Monday hit back at those questioning the honorary Doctor of Laws degree recently conferred by the Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Maynila (PLM) on President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr.

In a video message, Castro explained that “honoris causa” is an honorary degree bestowed upon a person who has attained a high-ranking position or has made significant contributions to a community or the nation.

“Marami kasi ang hindi nakakaunawa marahil ng katagang honoris causa. Ang mga tumutuligsa rito ay mga taong kung hindi man mapagmataas, ay mga kumakalaban sa Pangulo---the usual obstructionists at destabilizers, o ‘yung mga sumasakay lang sa nakikita sa social media, pero hindi nauunawaan ang totoong issue,” she said.

(Many perhaps don’t understand the term honoris causa. Those who criticize it are either arrogant people or those who oppose the President—the usual obstructionists and destabilizers, or simply those who jump on what they see on social media without understanding the real issue.)

“Ang titulong honoris causa ay isang honorary degree. Ito ay isang pagkilala o parangal para sa taong mataas ang naabot na posisyon, may mga mahahalagang naiambag sa komunidad o mga nagawa para sa bansa,” she added.

(The title honoris causa is an honorary degree. It is a form of recognition or an award bestowed upon an individual who has attained a high-ranking position and made significant contributions to the community or the nation.)
The Palace official emphasized that the honorary degree is not achieved through traditional education, by entering law school, or passing the Bar examinations.
She also underscored the need to clarify the matter for individuals being misled by others through fake news or sheer arrogance.
Marcos received the highest honorary degree conferred by the PLM---a Doctor of Laws, Honoris Causa---during the institution’s 58th commencement exercises on Thursday, August 27.
The President said he accepted the honor “with gratitude, mindful of the responsibility that comes with it.”
According to Castro, Filipinos should not forget the actions done by the President to be granted such a distinction, most especially maintaining the country’s rights in the West Philippine Sea.

“Ang pagpaputol ng 300-meter floating barrier na inilagay ng China Coast Guard sa Scarborough Shoal noong September 2023 para harangin ang ating mangingisda na makapasok at makapangisda sa traditional fishing lagoon ay isang gawain ng isang matapat na leader,” she said.

(Ordering the removal of the 300-meter floating barrier installed by the Chinese Coast Guard at the Scarborough Shoal in September 2023 to block our fishermen from entering and fishing in the traditional fishing lagoon was an act of a good leader.)
Castro said that Marcos also respects human life and due process, and fights against the abuse of power. She pointed out that he even initiated investigations into corruption issues.
She also said the President has ensured the country would not run out of fuel supplies amid the Middle East crisis, and also secured fertilizer supplies to protect farmers.

“Ang masagip ang isang kababayan mula sa death row, sentensyang pinataw ng ibang bansa; pagsagip sa 17 OFW sa Qatar sa kasong illegal assembly, at sa 24 Filipinos na nakadetained sa Eastern Siberia sa Russia. Ito ay nagawa ng Pangulo dahil sa maganda niyang relasyon sa leaders ng Qatar at Russia,” she added.

(The President saved a fellow Filipino from death row—a sentence imposed by a foreign nation, and rescued 17 OFWs in Qatar facing illegal assembly charges, as well as 24 Filipinos detained in Eastern Siberia, Russia. The President made this possible through his strong relationships with the leaders of Qatar and Russia.) — RSJ, GMA News

articles.title: Charo Santos joins NSYNC dance trend, surprises fans

items: Charo Santos surprises fans by joining the viral NSYNC dance trend, showing a playful side rarely seen from the veteran actress known for her dramatic roles.

blocks.text: Charo Santos dancing to NSYNC?
Well, why not?
The veteran actress, best known for serious and dramatic roles, recently joined the latest social media dance trend to “I Want You Back,” and fans were quick to react.
“Hindi tumatanda!”
“Kaya makipagsabayan!”
“Doesn’t look 70!”
Of course, it is not every day that Santos, whose name has long been associated with weighty drama and intense performances, pops up on social media dancing to an *NSYNC song.
But there she was.
And fans clearly enjoyed seeing this side of her.

The NSYNC Reel is not the only time Santos has been letting loose online. She is also having fun with her latest project, the short-form series “Rich Boyfriend’s Mom,” where she plays a wealthy mother determined to keep her son away from his girlfriend.

It is a different kind of role for an actress so closely associated with drama, but Santos leans into it with the same commanding presence audiences know her for, only this time, there is a lot more mischief involved.
And judging from the reactions online, viewers are having just as much fun watching her.

articles.title: DepEd urges parents to spot red flags to help curb school violence
articles.summary: The Department of Education (DepEd) is urging parents and guardians to take a more active role in preventing school violence, saying the home is the “first line of defense” against threats to…

blocks.text: Published August 31, 2026 3:22pm

The Department of Education (DepEd) is urging parents and guardians to take a more active role in preventing school violence, saying the home is the “first line of defense” against threats to learners.

Education Secretary Sonny Angara said in a statement on Monday that families should maintain regular communication with their children and coordinate closely with schools to identify warning signs before these escalate into violence or bullying.

“Hindi natin kayang solusyunan ang karahasan sa mga paaralan kung sa loob lang ng classroom tayo kumikilos. Ang tahanan ang ating unang depensa,” Angara said.(We cannot solve violence in schools if we act only inside the classroom. The home is our first line of defense.)
He urged parents to talk to their children daily, listen to what they are going through, and watch for changes in their behavior.

“Kailangan nating matutunang mapansin ang mga red flags at pagbabago sa kilos ng bata bago pa man umabot sa pananakit o bullying.”(We need to learn to recognize red flags and changes in a child’s behavior before these lead to violence or bullying.)

DepEd said it is expanding its Kaagapay Program, which provides parent communities with training on identifying red flags, managing behavioral concerns, and coordinating with school Child Protection Committees and guidance personnel.
The program is also being integrated with the Parent Effectiveness Service Program under Republic Act No. 11908, in coordination with the Department of Social Welfare and Development.

The department is conducting parent-and-teacher learner protection sessions from July to November in several regions, covering issues including bullying and cyberbullying, online sexual abuse and exploitation of children, online safety, and violent extremism.
DepEd said the sessions will also equip parents with technology-based protective tools and information on reporting and referral mechanisms when concerns arise.
At the school level, the department is coordinating with Parent-Teacher Associations and School Governing Councils to incorporate parent education into existing learner protection efforts.
Angara stressed that protecting children from violence requires cooperation among families, schools and communities.
“Shared accountability ang pagprotekta sa ating mga mag-aaral.”(Protecting our learners is a shared responsibility.) —RF, GMA News

articles.title: Man who told kin he'll end up at funeral parlor found floating in Ilocos river
articles.summary: LAOAG CITY, Ilocos Norte — The body of a man who had just been released from police custody was found floating on the Padsan River here on Sunday, August 30. Police identified the victim as…

blocks.text: LAOAG CITY, Ilocos Norte — The body of a man who had just been released from police custody was found floating on the Padsan River here on Sunday, August 30.
Police identified the victim as Herminigildo Gaño, a resident of Barangay 9, Sarrat, Ilocos Norte.
Gaño’s body was discovered floating in the river in Barangay 32-B, La Paz, prompting Barangay Captain Duldulao to alert the City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (CDRRMO).
The CDRRMO immediately deployed its Search and Rescue Team, Medical Team, and other personnel led by Dr. Melvin D. Manuel.
Rescuers, in coordination with the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG), recovered the body, which was reportedly clad a black striped shirt and black cargo shorts.
Dr. Janine Ramos conducted an examination before the remains were turned over to the Philippine National Police (PNP) for investigation.
Police said Gaño had been taken into custody in Sarrat on Aug. 28 because of his alleged violent behavior.
He was released the following day, but reportedly refused to leave with family members who had gone to fetch him.
Instead, Gaño allegedly ran toward the river and told his relatives that they would later find him at a funeral parlor in Laoag City.
The statement took on a grim significance after his body was recovered from the Padsan River the next day.
Police are investigating the circumstances surrounding Gaño’s death, including how he ended up in the river. It remained unclear if he drowned or if foul play was involved.
The CDRRMO said it would continue responding to emergencies in the city, particularly as persistent rains have affected the area.

articles.title: MGen to ensure energy security in Panay Island
articles.summary: ILOILO CITY—Amid the ongoing energy woes in the Visayas, Meralco PowerGen Corp. (MGEN) has committed to ensure energy security of Panay Island. “We are ready to contribute to Panay’s and the Visayas’…

blocks.text: ILOILO CITY—Amid the ongoing energy woes in the Visayas, Meralco PowerGen Corp. (MGEN) has committed to ensure energy security of Panay Island.
“We are ready to contribute to Panay’s and the Visayas’ energy security,” assured MGEN Thermal Energy Inc. President and Chief Executive Officer Arnel L. Santos.
MGEN Thermal (formerly Global Business Power Corp). operates three coal-fired power plants in Iloilo City under its subsidiary Panay Energy Development Corp. (PEDC).
While PEDC Unit 3 had an equipment failure last May 2026, it was able synchronize back to the Visayas grid its 150 megawatts (MWs) last July.
The restoration was seen as a relief for the Visayas, which had been under red and yellow alerts.
For months, there have been rotational power blackouts in Panay Island that particularly affected the city and province of Iloilo.
“Recent yellow and red alerts across the Visayas have brought energy security and power supply adequacy back into sharp focus,” said Santos during an August 28 media forum in Iloilo City.
During those times, Santos noted that PEDC Units 1 and 2 with combined capacity of 164 MWs as well as its two diesel-power plants in Aklan province with a 12-MW capacity were stable and operational.
“Their sustained performance reflects our broader commitment to keep our facilities available, dependable, and ready to contribute to Panay’s and the Visayas’ energy security,” explained Santos.
While having acknowledged the recent challenges faced by the Visayas grid, Santos said that MGEN Thermal Energy is working to do its share in preventing mass power disruptions.

“This reminds us that reliable power should never be taken for granted. Every power plant, transmission line, reserve facility, and supporting infrastructure plays a critical role in keeping the system stable and resilient,” noted Santos.
Joining Santos during the media forum were MGEN First Vice President and Panay Site Head Antonio Cabalhug Jr. and MGEN Retail Electricity Supplier Corp. Management Head Ralph Feliciano.

MANILA, Philippines – The Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) on Wednesday, August 19, directed district engineers of the Metro Manila 1st District Engineering Office to stop reclamation activities in a portion of Laguna de Bay in Taguig City.

The DPWH only publicly announced the cease and desist order on Sunday, August 30, over a week after DPWH chief Vince Dizon responded to the letter of Philippine Reclamation Authority (PRA) General Manager and CEO Cesar Siador Jr. to the agency.
In his letter to the DPWH dated August 17, Siador directed the DPWH to suspend reclamation activities in Laguna de Bay.

PRA also directed DPWH to submit proof of its authority to undertake the project’s reclamation component, including, where applicable, the appropriate PRA approval, National Economic and Development Authority Board approval, or other approvals required under the prevailing reclamation regulatory framework.

Senator Panfilo “Ping” Lacson said in a social media post on Monday, August 31 that “based on official records and our investigation, the total cost of Identified completed, ongoing (and suspended) DPWH Flood Control and Multi-Purpose Projects along the ‘illegal’ Laguna Lakeshore Reclamation Areas in Taguig City has so far reached ₱3.713 billion.”

Lacson previously flagged the reclamation of a portion of Laguna de Bay in Taguig City — the bailiwick of Senator Alan Peter Cayetano — over the lack of permits. Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the country, surrounded by cities in the southeast of Metro Manila, Laguna, and Rizal.

“Our Taguig City case study has opened a ‘cauldron of worms’ after my meeting with Philippine Reclamation Authority officials last night — from ghost slope protection projects to illegally reclaimed tracts of land covering Laguna Lake,” Lacson said in a post in early August.

Lacson also said PRA officials told him that Cayetano supposedly harassed them during budget deliberations in November 2025, when the budget of the Office of the President was taken up in plenary. The PRA is under the OP.

“The same officials likewise disclosed physical intimidation when they conducted an on-site inspection along C6 (Road) in the lakeshore area where the illegal reclamation activities are taking place,” Lacson said in a previous statement. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Palace warns vs theft of pumping station equipment: Don't sabotage the President's projects
articles.summary: Malacañang expressed dismay over the reported theft of pumping station equipment which prevented operations amid severe flooding in Manila during the heavy rains. Without the stolen components, the…

blocks.text: Malacañang expressed dismay over the reported theft of pumping station equipment which prevented operations amid severe flooding in Manila during the heavy rains.
Without the stolen components, the pumping station could not operate, causing further floods, Palace Press Officer and Communications Undersecretary Claire Castro said.
In a video statement on Monday, Aug. 31, Castro warned those behind the theft incident to stop sabotaging the President Marcos' projects.

"Reminder, warning sa mga nagnanakaw. Nakakalungkot ito dahil ginagawa ng Pangulo at ng DPWH (Department of Public Works and Highways), MMDA (Metropolitan Manila Development Authority) at iba pang ahensya ang lahat ng paraan para maibsan ang problema sa baha (Reminder, warning to those who are stealing: This is saddening because the President, the DPWH, the MMDA, and other government agencies are doing everything they can to help alleviate the problem of flooding)," CAastro said.

"Huwag ninyong isabotahe ang mga proyekto ng Pangulo. Magtulungan po tayo Lahat tayo ay Filipino, maging mabuting Filipino po tayong lahat (Do not sabotage the President’s projects. Let us work together. We are all Filipinos, so let us all be good Filipinos)," Castro added.

According to Castro, the President takes pride in the pumping stations that have been repaired and are now operational as these are among the reasons why floods subside more quickly in some areas of Metro Manila.
The Palace official also expressed frustration over the incident, saying the government has to find the replacement of the stolen components once again and spend for replacements and repairs.

"Pero dahil sa mga ninakaw ng mga halagang piyesa ng pumping stations hindi sila gagana. Gagastos tayo ulit para sa mga replacement na ito (But because valuable parts of the pumping stations have been stolen, they will not be able to operate. We will have to spend again to replace these stolen parts)," Castro said.

"Paano kung walang makuha agad na replacement? Hindi agad maiaayos ang mga ito na magdudulot na naman ng mabagan na paghupa ng baha (What if replacements cannot be obtained immediately? These pumping stations cannot be repaired right away, which could once again result in flooding taking longer to subside)," Castro lamented.

The Palace spokesperson stressed that the government’s efforts to prevent flooding are for everyone’s safety, urging people not to be selfish, as their actions could put lives, health, and property in communities at risk.

"Ang ginagawa ng Pangulo para sa kontrabaha ay para sa ating lahat. Huwag tayo maging makasarili. Buhay, kalusugan at ari-arian ang maaapektuhan dahil sa mga pagnanakaw na ito (What the President is doing to address flooding is for all of us. Let us not be selfish. Lives, health, and property could be affected by these acts of theft)," Castro said.
She warned those who are sabotaging the government that they will be hold accountable under the law.

"At sa lahat ng mga gumagawang pananabotahe na ito Kayo po ay hahabulin ng batas. Papanagutin po namin kayo dahil buhay at kabuhayan ang maaaring maapektuhan ng inyong mga makasariling gawain (And to all those carrying out these acts of sabotage: you will be held accountable under the law. We will hold you responsible because your selfish actions could put lives and livelihoods at risk)," Castro said.

Public Works and Highways Secretary Vince Dizon said the Sunog Apog Pumping Station in Tondo Manila failed to operate during the heavy rains after electrical wires for the generator and its Meralco connection were allegedly stolen.

articles.title: Man who murdered Molly Ticehurst unlikely to face life in jail, court hears
articles.summary: Justice Natalie Adams says she is troubled by expert evidence about rape allegations in slain woman’s police statement

blocks.text: Molly Ticehurst’s ex-boyfriend is unlikely to face a life sentence for her domestic violence murder, a crime which galvanised a national movement against gendered abuse.
Ticehurst, a 28-year-old childcare educator, was found dead in her home at Forbes, in the New South Wales central-west, in the early hours of 22 April 2024.
Her former boyfriend Daniel Billings broke into her bedroom and stabbed her 15 times in a ferocious attack that lasted less than a minute.

Billings had been charged with several counts of raping Ticehurst and a string of domestic violence offences just over two weeks before the killing, but he was freed on bail by a local court registrar the next day.
Ticehurst’s death became a flashpoint in the nation’s fight against domestic violence and led to legal changes in NSW, including tighter bail laws.
Billings, 31, who has pleaded guilty to murder, is will face court in Orange for a two-day sentence hearing from Thursday.
During a mention in the NSW supreme court on Monday, Adams raised the issue of a life sentence, although she noted she did not expect it to be requested.
Crown submissions before the court do not seek a life term, but they argue Billings should not get any discount on his sentence because his level of culpability is “extreme”.
Adams said there would probably be mitigating factors to consider when sentencing Billings, as there were in almost all cases.
“It’s difficult to identify what’s [legally] unique about this case,” she said.
But the judge said she was troubled with how to deal with expert evidence about Ticehurst’s police statement that she was repeatedly raped by Billings.
The sexual assault charges were dropped when Billings pleaded guilty to murder in November 2025 after 18 months of legal negotiations.
Billings always denied raping Ticehurst and developed a dark obsession with clearing his name in the lead-up to the murder.
“If I’m going to do the time, I may as well do the crime,” he said in a conversation with a friend soon before the murder, according to a statement of agreed facts before the court.
Adams said she could not ignore the rape allegations, despite the charges being dropped, when it came to sentencing Billings for murder.
“It was him seeing the police facts that set him to spiral,” the judge said.
Acting out of spite over the allegations could push his crime into another serious category, she said.
after newsletter promotion
“The sense of grievance about a perceived false allegation, there’s no getting around that,” Adams said.
“Whether it’s almost a public-justice type murder or domestic-violence type murder.”
Adams said it was possible all the elements to satisfy the legal definition of sexual assault were in Ticehurst’s account to police.
Changes to consent laws in NSW, which included affirmative language in the legislation, meant it was a crime where both parties “feel they’re telling the truth”.
“The only witness who could have told us is dead,” the judge said.
Billings, who has been in custody in the supermax wing of Goulburn jail since he was charged, will face court in person.
He will hear victim impact statements from the Ticehurst family, along with expert evidence about his mental state at the time of the murder.
A series of videos he made before and after the murder are also expected to be played to court.
Adams has indicated she will sentence Billings later in September.

articles.title: Nepal flood: Death toll crosses 900, thousands still missing
articles.summary: Rescue teams are racing to reach stranded people, even as nearly 4,800 remain missing. Meanwhile, mass burials have sparked controversy in Nepal.

image.caption: Multiple foreign rescue teams are assisting local authorities in reaching trapped hydropower workersImage: Niranjan Shrestha/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: The unprecedented flash flood in Nepal and Tibet has killed more than 900 people and left nearly 4,800 missing, authorities said Monday, as rescue efforts entered a sixth day.
"We are working in search and rescue of the stranded people from hills, settlements and river areas," Brigadier General Raja Ram Basnet, Nepal's army spokesman, said.
Nepalese authorities said many bodies have been recovered in southern Nepal, miles away from areas hardest hit by last Wednesday's floods.
Local media reported that some victims were being buried in mass graves, sparking controversy in the predominantly Hindu country, where cremation is the customary funeral rite.

articles.title: 2 NPA fighters yield in Misamis Oriental
articles.summary: BUTUAN CITY – Two armed New People’s Army (NPA) fighters yielded to police units in Misamis Oriental province recently. Regional Public Information Office chief of Police Regional Office 10 (PRO…

blocks.text: BUTUAN CITY – Two armed New People’s Army (NPA) fighters yielded to police units in Misamis Oriental province recently.

Regional Public Information Office chief of Police Regional Office 10 (PRO 10-RPIO) Police Major Joann G. Navarro, identified the rebel returnees as certain “Ka Dom”, 33 and “Ka Rhia”, 24, both of collapsing Platoon Lennon, Guerrilla Front (GF) 4B, Sub-Regional Committee 1 (SRC 1) of North Central Mindanao Regional Committee (NCMRC). They were presented to media on Monday, August 31.

Personnel of the 1001st Maneuver Company (MC), Regional Mobile Force Battalion 10 (RMFB 10), together with intelligence operatives of RMFB 10; 11th Special Action Company, 1st Special Action Battalion, Special Action Force; Regional Intelligence Unit 10 (RIU 10); Directorate for Intelligence–Mindanao Area Police Intelligence Office (DI-MAPIO); National Intelligence Coordinating Agency 10 (NICA 10); Magsaysay Municipal Police Station (MPS); Provincial Intelligence Unit (PIU); and 1st Provincial Mobile Force Company (PMFC), Misamis Oriental Police Provincial Office (MORPPO), jointly facilitated the voluntary surrender of the two rebels in Barangay Kibungsod, Magsaysay, Misamis Oriental, on Friday, Aug 28, and they were officially presented on Monday.
The two rebel returnees also yielded two shotguns and 12-gauge live bullets, as they pledged to help the government’s peace and development program, Navarro said.
They are now in the custody of the 1001st Maneuver Company, 10thRegional Mobile Force Battalion, in Lagonglong, Misamis Oriental, for custodial debriefing and individual profiling.
The surrendered firearms and ammunition are likewise under the custody of the same unit and will be turned over to the Regional Forensic Unit (RFU) for forensic examination.

Navarro added that their voluntary surrender was aligned with the Chief PNP’s focused agenda of strengthening internal security and supporting the government’s efforts to encourage members of armed groups to abandon the armed struggle, lay down their weapons, and return to the folds of the law.

Meanwhile, PRO 10 Director Police Brig. Gen. Nestor C. Babagay, Jr. emphasized that the peaceful surrender of these Communist Terrorist Group (CTG) members is a significant step toward lasting peace and security, urging those who remain in the armed movement to lay down their weapons, return to the folds of the law, and avail themselves of the government’s reintegration programs.

“Their decision to lay down their arms and return to the folds of the law is a positive step toward peace and a better future,” Brig. Gen. Babagay, Jr. said, adding “We encourage those who remain in the armed movement to choose peace, surrender voluntarily, and take advantage of the government’s reintegration programs”.

Recently, one city and eight towns in Northern Mindanao or Region 10 was formally declared under a state of Stable Internal Peace and Security (SIPS), marking the culmination of decades of efforts to end insurgency in the said areas.
The municipalities of Lugait, Manticao, Naawan, Initao, Libertad, Gitagum, Alubijid, and Opol, and El Salvador City are declared SIPS.

Maj. articles.title: DepEd orders schools to step up dengue, leptospirosis prevention amid rains
articles.summary: The Department of Education (DepEd) has ordered public schools nationwide to strengthen measures against dengue and leptospirosis as heavy monsoon rains and tropical cyclones increase the risk of…

blocks.text: The Department of Education (DepEd) has ordered public schools nationwide to strengthen measures against dengue and leptospirosis as heavy monsoon rains and tropical cyclones increase the risk of water- and mosquito-borne diseases.
Under its latest advisories, DepEd directed school heads, health personnel and staff to intensify sanitation, health monitoring and case reporting in schools.
Education Secretary Sonny Angara said learner and personnel safety must remain a priority during health and environmental emergencies.
“Katulad ng palaging paalala ng ating Pangulong Bongbong Marcos, hindi dapat nahihinto o naaalanganin ang edukasyon dahil sa mga banta sa kalusugan at kalamidad,” Angara said.
(As President Bongbong Marcos has always reminded us, education should not stop or be disrupted because of health threats and disasters.)
Angara also called on schools and families to work together in preventing the spread of disease.

“Ating ipinapanawagan sa ating mga school heads, guro, at magulang na magtulungan. Ang simpleng pagpapanatili ng kalinisan sa ating paligid, ang pagpuksa sa mga pinagmumulan ng lamok at pag-iwas sa pagbabad sa baha, ay malaking bagay upang mailayo ang ating mga kabataan sa sakit.”

(We are calling on our school heads, teachers and parents to work together. Simply keeping our surroundings clean, eliminating mosquito breeding grounds and avoiding exposure to floodwaters can go a long way in protecting our children from disease.)
DOH Enhanced 4S Strategy

DepEd instructed schools to implement the Department of Health’s Enhanced 4S Strategy against dengue: search and destroy mosquito breeding sites, secure self-protection, seek early consultation, and support fogging or spraying only when recommended by local health authorities.
Schools are also expected to regularly inspect classrooms, school grounds, gardens, toilets, storage areas, gutters and drainage systems for stagnant water.
The 4Ts—Taob, Taktak, Tuyo at Takip (turn over, drain, dry and cover)—under the 4 o’clock habit will likewise be incorporated into regular school sanitation activities.

Learners and school personnel are encouraged to wear long sleeves and pants when practicable, use mosquito repellents according to product instructions, and use physical barriers such as window screens and mosquito nets where appropriate.

Schools were also directed to provide age-appropriate health education and promptly refer individuals showing possible dengue symptoms, including sudden high fever lasting two to seven days, headache, pain behind the eyes, muscle and joint pain, abdominal pain or signs of bleeding.
Keep children out of floodwaters
DepEd also warned school communities about the risk of leptospirosis, which may result from exposure to floodwater or contaminated soil.
Schools were instructed to prohibit learners from swimming, wading or unnecessarily walking through floodwaters and muddy areas.

When exposure cannot be avoided, individuals should use protective gear such as boots and gloves, cover cuts or wounds with waterproof dressings, and immediately wash exposed skin with clean water and soap.
Those exposed to floodwater or potentially contaminated soil are advised to consult a health facility or local health office to determine whether post-exposure prophylaxis is needed.
DepEd stressed that antibiotics or post-exposure prophylaxis should not be self-administered and must only be taken upon the advice or prescription of a qualified health professional.

Schools must also strengthen rodent control and sanitation, including proper disposal of food waste and keeping classrooms, canteens and storage areas clean. Flooded school grounds must be cleaned, disinfected and assessed for safety before learners and personnel are allowed to return.
DepEd launches case-monitoring tool
To speed up reporting, DepEd has rolled out an automated Dengue and Leptospirosis Case Monitoring and Reporting Tool for schools, Schools Division Offices, Regional Offices and the Central Office.
Schools are required to encode reported cases according to DepEd’s internal reporting timelines, including within 24 hours of receiving information.
The department clarified that the monitoring tool is an internal DepEd mechanism and does not replace existing disease-surveillance and notification systems of the DOH and local health authorities.
DepEd urged parents, local governments and community partners to coordinate with schools in maintaining clean and safe learning environments amid the rainy season. — RSJ, GMA News

articles.title: VP Duterte trial: Prosecution ‘willing to wait’ for ill-stricken Fajarda
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines – The House prosecution panel will not rush former Department of Education (DepEd) special disbursing officer (SDO) Edward Fajarda to testify in Vice President Sara Duterte’s…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – The House prosecution panel will not rush former Department of Education (DepEd) special disbursing officer (SDO) Edward Fajarda to testify in Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial, counsel and House Deputy Speaker Rep. Paolo Ortega V said on Monday.
Fajarda’s schedule to testify on Duterte’s alleged misuse of confidential funds at DepEd was reset after he suffered a stroke on the lower back side of his brain, according to his physician.

“Sa tingin ko kailangan niya munang magpahinga. Wala namang may gusto na magkaroon ng sakit sa kalusugan… Mas maganda sana kung nasunod yung roster ng witnesses pero at this point kung mayroon siyang nararamdaman baka wala rin siyang maibigay at mahirapan siya kahit nga mag-attend lang,” Ortega shared in a press conference.

(“I think he needs to rest first. No one wants to have a health problem… It would have been better if the roster of witnesses had been followed but at this point if he has any feelings he might not be able to give anything and it would be difficult for him to even attend.”)
In the same forum, Manila 6th District Rep. Bienvenido Abante agreed with Ortega, adding that the prosecution team would be “willing to wait” until Fajarda is ready to testify.
“We’re sorry to hear on what happened to SDO Fajarda… I believe the prosecution team would be willing to wait until he is well enough to face the impeachment court,” Abante said.
He continued: “Hindi naman namin talaga pipilitin o mamadaliin yan. Kinakailangan talaga siya magpagaling muna.”
(We really won’t force or rush it. He really needs to get better first.)

Fajarda was initially scheduled to testify on August 25 to testify on his role as the DepEd’s SDO when Duterte was its secretary. He was supposedly tasked with disbursing and liquidating P112.5 million in secret funds from the the first to third quarters of 2023. /mr

blocks.text: MABALACAT CITY — Evacuation centers and staging areas in San Fernando, Pampanga are still sheltering 1,126 families, or 4,283 individuals, as of Monday, Aug. 31.

The San Fernando government said in a social media post that 52 families, or 198 people, are already settled in permanent evacuation centers, while 1,074 families, or 4,085 individuals, are currently staying in staging areas and temporary camps.
The evacuees left their homes due to deep flooding caused by persistent monsoon rains.
Staging areas and temporary camps include barangay halls, senior halls, covered basketball courts and public schools.

articles.title: Iran retaliates after first US strikes in a month
articles.summary: TEHRAN — Iran attacked US military targets in the Middle East on Monday in retaliation for the first American strikes on its territory in a month, in a fresh flare-up of the war that has…

blocks.text: TEHRAN — Iran attacked US military targets in the Middle East on Monday in retaliation for the first American strikes on its territory in a month, in a fresh flare-up of the war that has engulfed the region.

Tehran’s powerful Revolutionary Guards (IRGC) said they had responded to Sunday’s American attack by striking two US air bases with ballistic missiles in Washington-allied Jordan, causing “heavy damage”.
Jordan’s army said it had intercepted eight missiles, without stating their origin.
Tehran also claimed it targeted US military personnel at an air base in the United Arab Emirates and shot down a US drone over the Strait of Hormuz.
The flurry of attacks came after the United States said Sunday it had attacked Iranian rocket launchers on the small island of Larak in the strategic shipping lane.
Washington said its attacks were aimed at preventing Iran from placing more sea mines in the strait, days after the US announced it had completed clearing explosives from the waterway.
“US forces took limited, precise action against IRGC minelaying forces posing an imminent threat in the Strait of Hormuz,” the US military’s Central Command wrote on X.
Iran’s Guards said the US strikes resulted in “casualties” and that their subsequent attack on Jordan was “in response to the US-Zionist aerial aggression”.
The Iranian foreign ministry condemned the US attacks on Larak and justified the Jordan strikes as “legitimate defence”.
“We are not seeking war, but we will deliver a decisive response to the aggressors,” added Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian in a statement quoted by state TV.
Pezeshkian was speaking before traveling to Kyrgyzstan for a summit of a bloc that seeks to counter influence from the West, along with Russia’s President Vladimir Putin and China’s Xi Jinping.
The exchange of fire between the United States and Iran came shortly after their war hit its six-month mark, and at a time when hostilities had been subsiding.
In recent weeks, the administration of US President Donald Trump has prioritised “economic warfare” over military strikes.

Tehran has effectively blocked the Strait of Hormuz, the strategic sea lane through which one-fifth of the world’s oil passed before the US and Israel triggered the war with strikes on Iran on February 28.
“Last week, CENTCOM completed clearing sea mines from the strait’s international shipping routes,” said Navy Captain Tim Hawkins, a spokesman for US Central Command.
“US forces are monitoring the area closely and remain prepared to protect the free flow of commerce through this essential waterway,” he said.
Unpopular war
Diplomatic efforts, spearheaded by mediators including Pakistan and Qatar, have tried for months to bring an end to the war.

While a ceasefire was agreed in April and a memorandum of understanding towards a final peace deal was signed in June, no agreement has been forthcoming, and Washington has since declared “economic warfare” against Tehran.
A US naval counterblockade of Iranian ports is squeezing petrol supplies in Iran during a shortfall in domestic production.
The April ceasefire put an end to the most intense fighting, but sporadic attacks — mainly around the Strait of Hormuz — have dimmed prospects for a final peace agreement.

The last US strike on Iran before Sunday came on July 29 in response to “an attempted surprise attack on US forces” in the region, the US military said. Earlier in July, CENTCOM attacked Iran for 13 consecutive nights.
Throughout the war, Iran has fought back by striking US facilities and allies in the Gulf region, hitting targets in Kuwait, Oman, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, among others.
Its closure of the Strait of Hormuz has caused pain around the world in the form of price hikes and shortages of fertiliser and energy.
Both main crude oil contracts rose at least two percent on Monday.
The war is also deeply unpopular with the US public, with midterm elections looming in November that could overturn Republican control of Congress.
In a statement on Friday, US Senator Jack Reed criticised Trump over the war.
“Six months later, not a single objective has been achieved,” said Reed, the top Democrat on the Senate Armed Services Committee.
“Indeed, he has weakened our position in the Middle East and the world significantly.” /dl

articles.title: Ilocos Sur police condemn killing of 3-year-old boy
articles.summary: SAN ILDEFONSO, Ilocos Sur — The Ilocos Sur Police Provincial Office (ISPPO) has condemned the killing of a three-year-old boy in Barangay Lacong, Tagudin, and vowed to pursue the suspect. The boy…

blocks.text: SAN ILDEFONSO, Ilocos Sur — The Ilocos Sur Police Provincial Office (ISPPO) has condemned the killing of a three-year-old boy in Barangay Lacong, Tagudin, and vowed to pursue the suspect.
The boy died from a stab wound allegedly inflicted by his father inside their home in Tagudin on Aug. 28.
Initial reports said the victim’s grandmother and aunt heard the father berating the child at around 1 a.m. that day.
At about 11 a.m., the grandmother noticed that her grandson had not emerged from their room.
The grandmother found the child wrapped in a blanket. When she uncovered him, she saw that he had sustained a stab wound to the chest.
The child was immediately rushed to a hospital but was declared dead on arrival.
In a statement on Aug. 30, the ISPPO described the killing as “deeply disturbing and heartbreaking,” saying no child should experience violence.

“The death of a child is a tragedy that demands justice and accountability,” the police office said, adding that it would ensure the case was thoroughly investigated and that the person responsible faced the consequences of his actions.
The Tagudin Municipal Police Station has been directed to pursue all available leads and gather evidence to establish the circumstances surrounding the child’s death.
Police units were also ordered to exert all necessary efforts to locate the suspect.
The ISPPO assured the public that the investigation would be conducted with diligence while observing due process and the rule of law.
It also appealed to the public to remain vigilant and report any information that could help authorities locate the suspect or clarify the circumstances of the incident. /mcm

articles.title: South Korea’s medical tourism continues double-digit growth
articles.summary: SEOUL — Foreign card spending on medical services in South Korea jumped 66.5 percent in July from a year earlier, extending a rapid expansion in the country’s medical tourism industry. Foreign…

blocks.text: SEOUL — Foreign card spending on medical services in South Korea jumped 66.5 percent in July from a year earlier, extending a rapid expansion in the country’s medical tourism industry.
Foreign nationals spent 213 billion won ($145 million) on medical services and related products during the month, according to credit card-based data from the Korea Tourism Organization.
The increase follows annual growth of 65 percent in 2025 and 78.6 percent in 2024, suggesting the field is becoming a larger part of Korea’s inbound tourism economy.
Beyond beauty, beyond Asia

Korea has long been known for plastic surgery and dermatology, particularly among visitors from nearby countries such as China, Japan and Taiwan. In July, dermatology accounted for 54.9 percent of medical spending on foreign cards, while plastic surgery made up another 19.3 percent.
Ban Jun-seop, president of the Korean Association of Plastic Surgeons, said foreign patients accounted for as much as 70 percent of some plastic surgery clinics’ clientele.

But spending patterns show signs of diversification. The share of spending at pharmacies, for example, rose from 5 percent in March 2025 to 12.7 percent in July. Data from the Korea Health Industry Development Institute also shows demand spreading across a wider range of specialties and nationalities.
US nationals accounted for 24.1 percent of foreign patients who received health checkups in 2025, while patients from Mongolia and Kazakhstan featured prominently in other specialties.

“Patients from Japan, Taiwan, China, Singapore and Thailand tend to show a strong preference for dermatology and plastic surgery, while those from Kazakhstan, Canada and Mongolia often come to Korea for treatment of serious diseases such as cancer,” a Korea Health Industry Development Institute official said.
“Demand for treatment of serious diseases alone amounts to around 60,000 to 70,000 patients a year.”
Taking medical tourism beyond Seoul
The boom remains overwhelmingly concentrated in Seoul. In July, the capital accounted for 86.8 percent of total medical-related spending on foreign cards. Busan ranked second with just 6.4 percent.
That concentration has become a concern for local governments seeking to use medical tourism to encourage longer stays and generate additional spending at local businesses.
Experts say regions with fewer major medical institutions may be better off focusing on wellness and healthcare rather than trying to replicate Seoul’s medical tourism model.
Daegu, which ranked first outside the Seoul metropolitan area in the number of medical tourists in 2019, did not make the top five regions in terms of medical-related spending in July.

“It is practically impossible to distribute medical institutions across the country when they are already concentrated in Seoul,” Yoon Ji-hwan, a tourism professor at Kyung Hee University, told local media.
Yoon said Seoul could continue to focus on surgeries and procedures, while other regions develop healthcare tourism centered on wellness and traditional Korean medicine.
He said that would be a more realistic way to spread medical tourism beyond the capital. /dl

articles.title: ‘Breakthrough’ as Turkmenistan starts fixing ‘mindboggling’ methane mega-leaks
articles.summary:
Secretive state begins repairs on ageing facilities after being revealed as worst country for leaks of potent greenhouse gas

Turkmenistan has started plugging the mega-leaks of methane that…

blocks.text: Turkmenistan has started plugging the mega-leaks of methane that spew from its ageing oil and gas facilities, the latest UN data shows, in a move hailed as a breakthrough.

Methane, also called natural or fossil gas, is a potent greenhouse gas. It traps 80 times more heat than carbon dioxide and causes 25% of global heating today. Stopping leaks can be quick and cheap and, because methane breaks down in the atmosphere far quicker than CO2, this has a rapid impact, with some experts calling it the climate “emergency brake”.

The Guardian revealed in 2023 that Turkmenistan was the worst country for methane mega-leaks. Sources in Turkmenistan said this scrutiny was the “critical step” in leading the secretive and authoritarian government to engage with foreign partners.
A “super-emitter” leak, the escape of tonnes of methane per hour from a single valve or pipeline, heats the planet more than the emissions from a million SUVs or an entire coal-fired power station.
Turkmenistan had now stopped eight leaks by repairing corroded pipes, faulty wells and failing flares. The work was an “incredible first step”, said the UN, but much remained to be done.

blocks.caption: A satellite image of a methane leak in Turkmenistan's Lebap province, which was plugged in March after a corroded pipe was fixed. Illustration: UNEP’s International Methane Emissions Observatory

blocks.text: The UN Methane Alert and Response System (Mars) sent 192 alerts of methane plumes to Turkmenistan in the last year. The country had three of the six worst leaks detected in the world by Mars in last six months, and nine of the top 50.

Turkmenistan responded to about 20% of the alerts with on-the-ground information about the leaks and potential plans to fix them. In contrast, the US was sent the second highest number of alerts – 138 – but responded to none and had fixed no leaks in the last year. Other nations that failed to respond to any alerts were Iran, Russia and China.

The worst methane leak detected was an extraordinary leak in Mexico’s offshore oil and gas industry of 37 tonnes per hour, equivalent to the emissions of more than 7m SUVs. Mexico responded to all 23 Mars alerts in the last year, but had yet to complete a fix.

The plugging of leaks in Turkmenistan was encouraging, said Meghan Demeter, the programme manager of Mars, which is part of the UN Environment Programme. “These mitigation cases are a proof point of what can be done with satellite data, especially in situations like Turkmenistan, where there are a lot of detections. We’re seeing that the pipeline of satellite data to mitigation action works, and it can work quite quickly.”

“This is a breakthrough in terms of having real documented mitigation action,” she told the Guardian. “But it is not yet a breakthrough in the overall magnitude of emissions. Eight cases is an incredible first step, but there’s also a lot more sources in Turkmenistan that need to be addressed. We are in pretty constant communication and the response rate is growing month by month. We’re seeing steady progress.”

blocks.caption: A major methane leak detected in the US in June. Illustration: UNEP’s International Methane Emissions Observatory

blocks.text: In March 2023, the Guardian revealed Turkmenistan had the most super-emitting methane leaks in the world. It then revealed in May that the methane emissions alone from the nation’s two main fossil fuel fields caused more global heating in 2022 than the entire carbon emissions of the UK, which experts described as both “mind-boggling” and “infuriating”.

The findings caused a furore in Turkmenistan, prompting the government to engage with the UN, the EU and other nations and institutions to try to end the leaks, according to sources in the capital, Ashgabat. In December 2023, Turkmenistan joined the global methane pledge, two years after it had launched.

Turkmenistan has huge gas reserves and is a major supplier to China. Previously, leaks were ignored due to the enormous volumes on tap. But in November 2024, the first leak was fixed after a faulty well was repaired. The most recent repair, in March, was to a corroded pipeline. Turkmenistan’s ministry of foreign affairs and state companies Turkmenoil and Turkmengaz did not respond to a request for comment.

The most recent Mars data shows Kazakhstan, another former Soviet republic with ageing oil and gas infrastructure, has stopped eight leaks. However, the overall number of leaks in Kazakhstan is smaller, with 38 Mars alerts in the last year.

In total, Mars alerts have led to 43 leaks being sealed so far. Many have been straightforward fixes, with leaks plugged on the spot, while others required more planning and funding. One major leak now stemmed in Algeria had been running for almost 40 years, due to a faulty flare. Flares burn unwanted methane and turn it into CO2, a much less potent greenhouse gas.
after newsletter promotion

The previous US administration, under President Joe Biden, did engage with Mars and one small leak in New Mexico was fixed in 2024 after a pressure safety valve was repaired. But this engagement ended with the second presidency of Donald Trump. Last year, Trump called climate change “the greatest con job ever perpetrated on the world” at the UN general assembly.
Mexico, Brazil and Argentina have 100% response rates to Mars alerts, while Libya and Azerbaijan have high response rates.

blocks.caption: A methane leak at Baiji, in Iraq, was stopped in May after a corroded pipe was fixed. Illustration: UNEP’s International Methane Emissions Observatory

blocks.text: “Turkmenistan and Kazakhstan are home to some of the world’s most significant methane hotspots and their response to satellite alerts is much-needed good news in the global effort to minimise methane pollution,” said Dan Grossman, the vice-president at the Environmental Defense Fund.

“Stemming methane emissions from oil and gas operations is the quickest and most cost-effective method to reduce climate pollution available today,” he said. “Alerts only matter if they lead to action, and governments and industry must do a better job.”
The UN secretary general, António Guterres, has called for all countries to respond to 80% of alerts.

Demeter said: “We’re scaling up a lot in terms of the support that we can offer – knowledge building and technical support – and we are working alongside many partners. There are also a lot of requests for funding for direct mitigation.”

The Mars system uses artificial intelligence to analyse data from more than a dozen satellites and detect potential leaks, which are then checked by two layers of review by analysts. Verified leaks are then notified to the relevant government or company. Responses are recorded if they report on-the-ground information and an intention to plug the leak. If a leak is reported as fixed, Mars monitors the site until the data shows emissions have ended before recording it as a success.

articles.title: ‘Hot money’ swings to $3.94-billion outflow at end-July as foreign investors turn cautious
articles.summary: Foreign investors pulled more money out of Philippine financial assets than they brought in during the first seven months of 2026, reversing the net inflows a year ago as geopolitical tensions,…

blocks.text: Foreign investors pulled more money out of Philippine financial assets than they brought in during the first seven months of 2026, reversing the net inflows a year ago as geopolitical tensions, inflation risks, and volatile markets prompted greater caution toward emerging-market (EM) assets.

The latest Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) data showed that foreign portfolio investments, commonly called “hot money,” registered net outflows of $3.94 billion from January to July, a turnaround from the $2.25 billion in net inflows recorded in the same period last year.

Union Bank of the Philippines (UnionBank) chief economist Ruben Carlo O. Asuncion said the reversal reflected greater caution among foreign investors toward riskier EM assets amid heightened global uncertainty.

Asuncion said that while the Philippines continues to attract foreign portfolio investments, “overall withdrawals have outweighed new placements this year as investors respond to heightened geopolitical tensions, elevated inflation risks, volatile financial markets, and concerns over global growth.”

He said portfolio flows are largely influenced by global investor sentiment rather than domestic conditions, adding that the net outflows do not necessarily signal weaker confidence in the Philippines but reflect investors’ increased caution and preference for flexibility amid global uncertainty.
The weakening trend was also evident in July, when hot money recorded a net inflow of just $66 million—the smallest monthly net inflow so far this year and the lowest in three months.

While July marked the third consecutive month of net inflows following $232 million in May and $170 million in June, the figures showed that the monthly surplus had steadily narrowed during the three-month period.
The July net inflow was also a fraction of the $743 million recorded in the same month last year. The highest monthly net inflow so far this year was February’s $284 million.

Hot money refers to foreign investments registered with the BSP through authorized agent banks (AABs) that can be readily moved into and out of financial markets depending on investors’ appetite for risk and changes in economic, financial, or political conditions.
These portfolio investments are called hot money because of their short-term and highly liquid nature, making them more susceptible to rapid withdrawals during periods of heightened uncertainty.

Registered foreign portfolio investments may be placed in listed securities, peso-denominated government securities (GS), time deposits with maturities of at least 90 days, other debt instruments, unit investment trust funds (UITFs), exchange-traded funds (ETFs), and Philippine depositary receipts (PDRs).

From January to July, gross outflows surged to $19.55 billion, exceeding the $15.61 billion in gross inflows. In the same period last year, gross inflows stood at $14.44 billion, while gross outflows were lower at $12.16 billion.

Both major asset classes recorded net outflows during the seven-month period. Government debt securities posted net outflows of $2.21 billion, while listed securities on the Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) registered net outflows of $1.73 billion.
This was a reversal from the same period last year, when GS generated net inflows of $3.74 billion, which more than offset the $1.46 billion in net outflows from listed securities.

articles.title: 'Moonies' church leader jailed for two years over bribery offences
articles.summary: Han Hak-ja, 83, gave South Korea's former first lady two Chanel bags and a diamond necklace, a court found.

blocks.text: The leader of the controversial Unification Church has been sentenced to two years in prison for bribing South Korea's former first lady and other political funding offences.
A court found that Han Hak-ja's church gave Kim Keon Hee, the wife of ousted president Yoon Suk Yeol, two Chanel bags and a diamond necklace, together worth 80 million won ($57,900; £42,500).
Earlier this year, Kim was sentenced to 20 months in jail for accepting bribes from the church.
Han, the 83-year-old widow of the Unification Church's founder Sun Myung Moon, had repeatedly denied the allegations, calling them "false".
A special counsel team appointed to the case said Kim received the luxury products from the church between April and July 2022, in exchange for business and political favours.

The prosecutors said the probe was the first time the authorities have confirmed the church's attempt at buying influence in politics, and released photos of $19m (£14m) worth of cash found in Han's personal safe.
South Korea's former first lady admitted to receiving Chanel bags, but said she later returned them without using them.
Kim made a public apology when she appeared for questioning last August: "I am truly sorry that a nobody like me has caused concern to the people."
The Unification Church, known formally as The Family Federation for World Peace and Unification, was founded in South Korea in the 1950s by Sun Myung Moon, who proclaimed himself the messiah.
The church is probably best known for the mass weddings where thousands of couples were married by Han and her late husband and founder Sun Myung Moon in a stadium.

Critics have described the group as "cult-like". Lawyers have accused it of coercing devotees, known colloquially as "Moonies" after its founder, to donate large sums of money. "Moonies" is a term used by critics that many church members find offensive.

The Unification Church had come under the spotlight in Japan after the assassination of the country's former leader Shinzo Abe. The alleged assassin blamed the group for bankrupting his family and held a grievance against Abe for allegedly promoting it.
The church has boasted extensive links to politicians in Seoul, Tokyo, and even in Washington. Various politicians sent video message to its 2021 event congratulating the church's new think tank.
The list included US President Donald Trump, former US Vice-President Mike Pence, Shinzo Abe, as well as the mayors of Seoul and Busan.
The group is banned in parts of the world, including Singapore. In Japan, it has been ordered to dissolve.

blocks.text: La Salle's Luis Pablo (UAAP Media)

The University Athletic Association of the Philippines (UAAP) has decided to only hold five game days in September as several of its student-athletes will be playing for Gilas Pilipinas squads in the coming 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games in Japan and the FIBA 3x3 Under-23 World Cup in Wuhan, China.

With UAAP Season 89 men’s basketball firing off on Sunday, Sept. 13, the league adjusted its final schedule to give way for the cagers who were selected to don the national colors on international competitions.

“We have always believed that the UAAP’s mission goes beyond the competition. We are here to develop student-athletes who can represent our schools, but we are equally proud when they get the opportunity to represent the country,” said this season’s president Mark Molina of Far Eastern University.
“The UAAP will always support all our national teams, and we are willing to adjust our schedules whenever necessary to give our student-athletes the opportunity to serve the Philippines,” he added.
The UAAP is set to hold games on the 16th, 26th and 30th at Mall of Asia Arena, and on the 13th and 19th at the Smart Araneta Coliseum.
Reigning champion De La Salle faces National University in the main event on Sept. 13.

La Salle’s Luis Pablo and Doy Dungo together with UST’s Koji Buenaflor are called up for the men's 3x3 team of the Asian Games slated Sept. 21 to 25, while Kacey Dela Rosa and Co. banner the women’s 5-on-5 basketball team.

articles.title: Grade 2 pupil dies after family is swept away by strong current at Cagayan River
articles.summary: SAN PABLO, Isabela – A seven-year-old Grade 2 pupil drowned after she and two family members were swept away by a strong current while bathing in the Cagayan River here on Friday, August 28, a…

blocks.text: SAN PABLO, Isabela – A seven-year-old Grade 2 pupil drowned after she and two family members were swept away by a strong current while bathing in the Cagayan River here on Friday, August 28, a belated report from authorities said.
The victim was identified only as Zheille, a resident of this town.
Police said the family was in the river in Barangay Auitan at around 5:35 p.m. when they were reportedly swept away by the strong current.
Two of the child’s relatives were rescued, but Zheille disappeared in the rushing water.
The San Pablo Municipal Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (MDRRMO) received a request for assistance at around 6:45 p.m. from Barangay Auitan Chairperson Margie Ramos.
MDRRMO Officer Roseman B. Tumaliuan immediately coordinated with the San Pablo Municipal Police Station and the Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP), while Search and Rescue Team 210 was deployed.
Barangay officials, residents, and volunteers joined rescuers in the search, which continued through the night.
The operation resumed at around 5 a.m. on August 29, with rescuers scouring the Cagayan River and downstream areas.

The San Pablo MDRRMO also coordinated with the Isabela Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (PDRRMO) and neighboring local government units along the river. A Water Search and Rescue (WASAR) team was dispatched to reinforce the operation.

However, before the WASAR team could reach San Pablo, the child’s body was found and recovered at around 10:16 a.m. in Barangay Namabbalan, Tuguegarao City, Cagayan — far downstream from where she was last seen.
Authorities said the tragedy again underscored the deadly danger posed by strong river currents, particularly during the rainy season.
They urged parents and guardians to closely watch children and avoid swimming or entering rivers when water levels are high and currents are strong.
The public was also advised to stay away from deep or unfamiliar waters, heed warnings from local authorities, and never underestimate the power of river currents.

In December 2024, three children aged eight, nine, and 10 also drowned in the Cagayan River in Barangay Annafunan, Tumauini, Isabela, according to a Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) report.

articles.title: Ex-NPA leader falls to authorities in Nueva Ecija
articles.summary: CAUAYAN CITY, Isabela — The remaining pillar of what was once a formidable communist rebel structure operating in the Cordillera and Ilocos regions has fallen into the hands of authorities. John Lee…

blocks.text: CAUAYAN CITY, Isabela — The remaining pillar of what was once a formidable communist rebel structure operating in the Cordillera and Ilocos regions has fallen into the hands of authorities.

John Lee Hondrado, alias “Lig-on,” an alleged remnant of the Ilocos-Cordillera Regional Committee (ICRC) and former leader of the dismantled Kilusang Larangang Gerilya (KLG) North Abra, was arrested in Nueva Ecija in what security forces described as a major blow to the remaining network of the group.

The Philippine Army’s 5th Infantry Division (5ID) said Hondrado was arrested in Barangay Parista, Lupao, Nueva Ecija, on August 21 in a joint operation with the Philippine National Police (PNP), including the Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (CIDG).

The military described Hondrado as the last remaining member of the ICRC, a development that could signal the final collapse of the regional communist structure that once operated across parts of the Cordillera and Northern Luzon.
Hondrado, also identified as a former leader of KLG North Abra, had allegedly remained at large even after the guerrilla unit was dismantled.
Authorities arrested him while serving warrants for attempted homicide and violations of laws on the illegal manufacture, sale, acquisition, possession, and ownership of firearms and ammunition.
His arrest came five months after security forces launched a sweeping crackdown against alleged ICRC members.

On March 11, authorities arrested 10 alleged active members of the ICRC in simultaneous operations in Fairview, Quezon City, and Tarlac City. The suspects were allegedly linked to rebel operations in Abra, Kalinga, and Apayao.

The arrests were followed by the surrender of two other high-ranking communist terrorist group officials in Tabuk City, Kalinga, bringing the total number of persons accounted for in the earlier operations to 12.

Among those identified was Gabriel Kennedy Lao-ing Bangibang, described as a former KLG Baggas secretary and National Democratic Front of the Philippines (NDFP) consultant. He is now detained at the BJMP-Kalinga District Jail.

Also identified were Theresa Falitnang Forag, an alleged ICRC member from Abra, and Javar Anglao Sugao, described as a former KLG Baggas intelligence officer and alleged vice commanding officer of the New People’s Army (NPA) in Kalinga.
Other alleged members included Renato Ginez, Rani Francella Tuazon, Marc Arriane Mendiola y Tolentino, and Bobby Calsiyao Yag-ao, a former KLG Baggas member and alleged NPA Abra assistant medic.
The earlier suspects were wanted for offenses ranging from attempted and frustrated murder to qualified trafficking in persons and illegal possession of firearms and explosives.
With Hondrado now in custody, government security forces believe they may have closed in on what was left of the ICRC’s once-sprawling network.
However, authorities are not yet declaring the fight over.

Security forces continue to track possible underground operatives and supporters and are monitoring any attempt to rebuild or revive dismantled communist structures in the Cordillera and Northern Luzon.

articles.title: Negros Oriental top cop, 6 police chiefs sacked for failure to stop illegal gambling
articles.summary: BACOLOD CITY - The Police Regional Office-Negros Island Region (PRO-NIR) has relieved seven police commissioned officers, including the Negros Oriental police director over its one-strike policy…

blocks.text: BACOLOD CITY - The Police Regional Office-Negros Island Region (PRO-NIR) has relieved seven police commissioned officers, including the Negros Oriental police director over its one-strike policy (OSP) against illegal gambling.

Police Col. Lito Patay, deputy regional director for operations of PRO-NIR, was designated in concurrent capacity as officer-in-charge (OIC) of Negros Oriental police, following the relief of Police Col. Timmar Alam, Negros Oriental police director.

The six sacked police chiefs were Police Lt. Col. Joeson Parallag, OIC of Bayawan City Police Station; Police Lt. Col. Romeo Cubo, OIC of Guihulngan City Police Station; Police Major Mary Jean Gutierrez, OIC of Sibulan Municipal Police Station; Police Capt. James Taylor Pineda, OIC of Pamplona Municipal Police Station; Police Capt. Arturo Marfil III, OIC of Tayasan Municipal Police Station; and Police Capt. Joesanne Magalso, OIC of Ayungon Municipal Police Station.

Their vacated posts were assumed respectively by Police Lt. Col. Ronoel Fungo, Police Lt. Col. Nerito Lobrido, Police Major Antonio De Leon Jr., Police Capt. Roldan Maraña, Police Capt. Cecile Jakosalem Mingay, and Police Capt. Berwyn Soreño.

The relief stemmed from simultaneous operations conducted by the Regional Special Operations Group (RSOG), which resulted in the arrest of six individuals, who were allegedly caught in the act of soliciting and collecting bets for illegal numbers games.

The operations were conducted from 10:14 a.m. to 1:34 p.m. on Friday, August 28, which resulted in the recovery of betting slips, improvised betting receipts, claim stubs, notebooks containing various number combinations, ballpens, P550 bet money, and P620 cash believed to be proceeds from illegal gambling activities.

In a statement, Police Brig. Gen. Romano Cardiño, PRO-NIR director, emphasized that the OSP is a clear manifestation of the Philippine National Police (PNP) leadership’s uncompromising stance against illegal gambling and all forms of unlawful activities.
The regional director further stressed that the relief of the concerned commanders should serve as a stern warning to all police units and personnel that accountability accompanies leadership.
He said that commanders are expected to ensure that illegal activities are prevented, detected, and decisively addressed.

Police commanders and personnel throughout the region were directed to intensify intelligence gathering, sustain anti-illegal gambling operations, and ensure the strict enforcement of all laws against illegal gambling.

“Command responsibility is fundamental in the performance of every police officer,” Cardiño said, adding that the presence and continued operation of illegal gambling activities within an area of responsibility cannot be tolerated.

“This is not merely about conducting arrests. It is about ensuring that our commanders remain vigilant, proactive, and fully accountable for what happens within their respective areas of responsibility,” he said.

“The OSP will be implemented fairly, firmly, and without exception,” he stressed pursuant to the directive of PNP Chief Police Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr., to intensify its campaign against illegal gambling and institute decisive administrative action against police commanders who failed to stop its proliferation, particularly in Negros Oriental.
The PRO-NIR assured the public that the campaign against illegal gambling will continue relentlessly.

Last June, the PRO-NIR implemented first the OSP with the relief of Police Major Fortunato Sabio Villafuerte, former chief of Sibulan Municipal Police Station. He was replaced by Gutierrez, who was among the recent sacked police officers for the same reason.

articles.title: EJ Obiena impresses anew with gold-medal win in Germany
articles.summary: Two-time Olympian EJ Obiena impressed once more by posting a 5.82-meter performance to complete a gold-medal win in the 2026 Internationales Stadionfest (ISTAF) in Berlin, Germany Sunday, Aug. 30.…

blocks.text: At A Glance

items: Two-time Olympian EJ Obiena impressed once more by posting a 5.82-meter performance to complete a gold-medal win in the 2026 Internationales Stadionfest (ISTAF) in Berlin, Germany Sunday, Aug. 30.

blocks.text: EJ Obiena (EJ Obiena / Facebook)
Two-time Olympian EJ Obiena impressed once more by posting a 5.82-meter performance to complete a gold-medal win in the 2026 Internationales Stadionfest (ISTAF) in Berlin, Germany Sunday, Aug. 30.
Coming off a fifth-place finish at Diamond League’s Zurich leg in Switzerland, the 30-year-old Obiena bounced back after clearing 5.82 meters to conquer the 10-man field before a huge German crowd.
“5.82m here in Berlin for the [gold]. Thank you @istaf_berlin for having me. Hope to see you again next year!!! [Para sa bayan],” Obiena wrote on his social media post.

After pulling off a 5.90-meter performance a few days ago, the pride of Tondo, Manila topped the event with Belgian Ylio Philtjens (5.72m) and Frenchman Robin Emig (5.72m) settling for the silver and bronze honors, respectively.
It marked Obiena’s ninth gold this year.
Obiena is gearing up for his title defense in the 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games in Japan.
Obiena’s 5.90-meter effort in Zurich led to his qualification in the 2027 World Athletics Championships set in Beijing, China.
